## Summary This PR adds the `rehype-raw` plugin to enable proper rendering of raw HTML content within markdown. This allows markdown content to include HTML elements that are properly parsed and rendered instead of being escaped. ## Key Changes - **Added `rehype-raw` dependency** (`7.0.0`): Rehype plugin for parsing raw HTML in markdown - **Updated Markdown component**: Integrated `rehype-raw` as a rehype plugin in the ReactMarkdown configuration - **Package organization**: Reordered `react-markdown` in dependencies (no functional change) ## Architecture Benefits - **Enhanced content flexibility**: Allows agents and users to include HTML elements in markdown output for richer formatting - **Better interoperability**: Handles mixed HTML/Markdown content commonly found in AI-generated responses - **Maintains security**: Works alongside existing sanitization in the markdown component ## Technical Details The `rehype-raw` plugin is added to the `rehypePlugins` array in the `Markdown` component: ```typescript {sanitizedChildren} ``` This enables HTML elements like `
`, ``, `
`, etc. to be properly parsed and rendered within markdown content. ## Testing - ✅ Build passes: `pnpm build` - ✅ Type checking passes: `pnpm typecheck` - ✅ Linting passes: `pnpm lint` - ✅ Dependencies installed: `pnpm install` ## Related Issues This enhances markdown rendering capabilities for agent outputs that may include HTML formatting.

body:
### Multi-Step Event Creation Wizard

- **Category Selection**: Visual category cards with background images
- **Event Details**: Title, description, and tag selection with client-side search
- **Media Management**: Image upload, editing (crop, rotate, brightness/contrast), reordering images with drag-and-drop
- **Date & Time Selection**: Start/end datetime pickers with validation logic
- **Location System**:
    - Single place selection with Google Maps preview
    - Route planning with multiple waypoints and polyline visualization
    - Online events with meeting URL input and quick-launch buttons (Zoom, Discord, Meet)
- **Capacity & Audience**: Custom stepper for person count with unlimited option and +18 age restriction toggle
- **Preview & Submit**: Comprehensive event card preview before final submission

### Location & Place System

- Google Places SDK integration with autocomplete search
- Debounced search (300ms) with location-biased results
- Geolocation permissions handling
- Address component extraction (country, city, area)
- Interactive Google Maps with markers and polylines

### Media Handling

- Image picker (Camera/Gallery support)
- Image compression (PNG to JPEG) before upload using `flutter_image_compress`
- Aspect ratio management (0.80 - 1.91 range)
- Firebase Storage integration with file validation
- Transactional image operations for data consistency
- Carousel view with dot/text indicators

### Tagging System

- Tag entity with `TagType` enum
- Firebase-backed tag repository
- Client-side tag search and filtering
- Visual tag selection UI

### State Management

- Centralized `EventCreateFormState` with Riverpod notifier
- Form validation at each step
- Image state management (add, remove, reorder)
- Action providers for async operations (create, update, delete)
- Proper error handling with `Result` and `EventFailure` types

## **Architecture**

### Domain Layer

- **Entities**: `Event`, `EventImage`, `Tag`, `LocationData`, `CapacityRange`, `PlaceSuggestion`
- **Enums**: `EventType`, `EventCategory`, `TagType`
- **Use Cases**:
    - Event: `CreateEvent`, `UpdateEvent`, `DeleteEvent`, `GetEvent`, `GetEvents`
    - Images: `AddEventImage`, `RemoveEventImage`
    - Tags: `GetTags`
    - Places: `SearchPlaces`, `GetPlaceDetails`

### Data Layer

- **Firebase Integration**:
    - Firestore for event data with CRUD operations
    - Firebase Storage for image uploads with size/type validation
    - Google Places SDK for location services
- **Models**: `EventModel`, `EventImageModel`, `TagModel` with Firestore serialization
- **Repositories**: `EventRepository`, `TagRepository`, `EventPlaceRepository`
- **Services**: `EventRemoteService`, `EventStorageService`, `EventPlaceService`, `LocationProvider`

### Presentation Layer

- **Pages**: Category, Details, Media, Date, Place, Person, Preview
- **Widgets**:
    - `EventCreateScaffold` - Reusable scaffold with progress bar
    - `EventProgressBar` - Visual step indicator with fade transitions
    - `EventPreviewCard` - Comprehensive event preview with expandable description
    - `ImageSlider` - Custom carousel with indicators
    - `CapacityStepper` - Custom stepper for person count
    - `LocationSearchBar` - Debounced search with suggestions
    - Various editors for place page : `SinglePlaceEditor`, `RouteEditor`, `OnlinePlaceEditor`
- **State Management**: Action providers, view models, form state notifiers

## **Technical Improvements**

- Parallel Firebase initialization with SharedPreferences loading
- Image compression before upload
- Debounced search queries
- Null safety throughout

## **Dependencies Added**

- `cloud_firestore` - Firebase database
- `firebase_storage` - Image storage
- `flutter_image_compress` - Image compression
- `flutter_google_places_sdk` - Places API
- `google_maps_flutter` - Maps widget
- `geolocator` - Location services
- `envied` - Environment variable management

## **Description**

<!--
Write a short description of the changes included in this pull request, also include relevant motivation and context. Have in mind the following questions:
1. What is the reason for the change?
2. What is the improvement/solution?
-->

Rive animations were appearing blurry in the MetaMask extension UI. This was caused by LavaMoat policy overrides that restricted access to devicePixelRatio and other viewport-related globals for the Rive packages.

This PR removes the unnecessary LavaMoat policy overrides for:
- @rive-app/canvas - removed devicePixelRatio: false restriction
- @rive-app/react-canvas - removed the entire override section (which restricted devicePixelRatio, innerHeight, innerWidth, matchMedia, etc.)

By removing these overrides, the Rive packages can now properly access devicePixelRatio to render animations at the correct resolution for the user's display, preventing blur on high-DPI/Retina screens.

Jira Link: https://consensyssoftware.atlassian.net/browse/SL-370

body:
The reason is that currently the microdnf command failes with:
  microdnf: symbol lookup error: /lib64/librpm_sequoia.so.1: undefined symbol: EVP_PKEY_verify_message_init, version OPENSSL_3.4.0

This is a bug with a mismatching version of the rpm-sequioa and openssl. The bug report (https://issues.redhat.com/browse/RHEL-130960) mentions that explicitly updating openssl-libs helps.

author: martijnrusschen
body:
Fixes https://github.com/Hacker0x01/react-datepicker/issues/5459

When typing a partial date (e.g., just "2014") in the input field, the calendar now navigates to that year/month even though the full date cannot be parsed. This restores the v7 behavior where users could search through the calendar by typing partial dates.

- Add parseDateForNavigation() to extract year/month from partial input
- Update handleChange to use partial navigation when full parse fails
- Respect minDate/maxDate constraints when navigating
- Handle invalid input gracefully (returns null, calendar stays put)

body:
Thanks for your contribution and we appreciate it a lot. The following instructions would make your pull request more healthy and more easily get feedback. If you do not understand some items, don't worry, just make the pull request and seek help from maintainers.

Motivation
I’m running the MinerU API service on Kubernetes and found several issues:

There is no proper liveness/readiness probe endpoint.
When using the /docs page for API testing, calling parse_file blocks the entire event loop, causing all other endpoints to become unresponsive.

During testing, memory usage spikes when loading PDF images.
The service starts 4 worker processes by default, and memory usage doubles or even triples.
With Kubernetes memory limits, the container frequently gets OOMKilled.

Modification
Therefore, I made the following improvements:

Added a lightweight health check endpoint (/health)
More suitable for Kubernetes probes than /docs.

Refactored parse_file into a non-blocking API
It no longer blocks the async event loop.
To prevent request overload, I added a configurable concurrency limit: MINERU_CONCURRENT_REQUEST_NUM

Made the PDF image loading worker count configurable
The default is now 1 instead of 4, which prevents unnecessary memory duplication and avoids K8s OOM issues.I added a configurable env: MINERU_PDF_LOAD_PROCESS_NUM

BC-breaking (Optional)
Does the modification introduce changes that break the backward compatibility of the downstream repositories?
If so, please describe how it breaks the compatibility and how the downstream projects should modify their code to keep compatibility with this PR.

Use cases (Optional)

author: copilot
body:
Users reported Cloudflare timeout errors despite correct DNS setup and working SSH. The issue: overly broad error detection triggered on any "gateway" + "timeout" response, and error messages incorrectly implied SSH/VPS connectivity problems when the actual cause was Cloudflare's 100-second HTTP timeout being exceeded during long deployments.

## Changes

**Error Detection (`app.js`)**
- Require "cloudflare" string presence in responses (previously matched any gateway timeout)
- Add CF-Ray header and error codes 522/524 detection
- Extract duplicate logic to `isCloudflareErrorPage()` helper function

```javascript
// Before: false positives on any gateway timeout
const isCloudflareError = 
  (lowerResponseText.includes('gateway') && lowerResponseText.includes('timeout'));

// After: specific Cloudflare identifiers required
function isCloudflareErrorPage(responseText) {
  const lower = responseText.toLowerCase();
  return (
    (lower.includes('cloudflare') && (lower.includes('504') || lower.includes('524') || lower.includes('522'))) ||
    lower.includes('cf-ray')
  );
}
```

**Error Messages (`app.js`)**
- Clarify HTTP request timeout vs SSH connection failure
- Explain admin panel access through Cloudflare causes timeout
- Provide actionable solutions: direct IP access, pre-install dependencies, or CLI deployment

**Documentation (`CLOUDFLARE_DNS_GUIDE.md`)**
- Add "Understanding Cloudflare timeout errors" section distinguishing real vs false positives
- Document root cause: deployments exceeding Cloudflare's 100s HTTP timeout
- Three solutions with security considerations (HTTP vs HTTPS warning)
- Separate troubleshooting for non-Cloudflare SSH errors (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT)

## Key Insight

The error isn't about DNS configuration—it's about the admin panel being accessed through Cloudflare while deployments take >100 seconds. The HTTP request times out before the SSH operation completes, despite SSH working correctly.

- Remove daemon=True to prevent premature thread termination

- Add proper timeout handling and queue cleanup

Fixes #14

This change addresses the issue where codex MCP calls would hang indefinitely even though codex CLI completed successfully and returned results visible in the web UI. The fix detects the turn.completed event and actively terminates the process after a short delay to ensure output is complete.

Implements complete androidTest suite for `CollectionItemDao` covering all DAO operations with in-memory database testing.

## Test Coverage (16 tests)

- **CRUD operations**: insert, insertAll, getCollection, observeCollection, deleteAll, replaceCollection
- **Sorting**: alphabetical by name, SQLite BINARY collation behavior
- **Upsert semantics**: OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE for single and bulk operations
- **Flow emissions**: initial state, updates after mutations, transactional replacements
- **Edge cases**: null fields, empty collections, idempotent operations

## Changes

**`app/src/androidTest/java/app/meeplebook/core/database/CollectionItemDaoTest.kt`**
- In-memory Room database with `allowMainThreadQueries()` for test isolation
- Helper factory with ergonomic parameter order: `createTestEntity(gameId, name, subtype, ...)`
- Null defaults for optional parameters to surface test intent

**`app/build.gradle.kts`**
- Added `androidTestImplementation` for `kotlinx-coroutines-test` and `room-testing`
- Separated unit test vs instrumented test dependencies with clarifying comments

## Example Usage

```kotlin
@Test
fun upsertReplacesExistingItem() = runTest {
    dao.insert(createTestEntity(1, "Original", BOARDGAME, 2000))
    dao.insert(createTestEntity(1, "Updated", BOARDGAME_EXPANSION, 2020))
    
    val result = dao.getCollection()
    assertEquals(1, result.size)
    assertEquals("Updated", result[0].name)
}
```

No mocks—tests execute actual SQL against Room's in-memory database.

## Description
This PR adds validation for the Project resource name to ensure it does not exceed 53 characters.
Project names are used as prefixes for generated Kubernetes resource names. These names later get a hashed suffix, and exceeding the Kubernetes 63-character limit would cause resource creation failures.

## Why do we need this:
Without this validation, users can create Project objects with names too long to be safely used as base names for generated resources. This results in broken deployments and hard-to-debug errors.

## What was changed:
- Added x-kubernetes-validations rule to CRD projects.deckhouse.io (v1alpha2).
- Validation rule: size(self.metadata.name) <= 53.
- Added user-facing message explaining the restriction.

author: copilot
body:
Implements a complete air mouse system using ESP32-C3, MPU6050 gyroscope, and ADXL335 accelerometer with AI-based gesture recognition over BLE HID.

**Simplified single-file Arduino structure** - All code consolidated into `ai_mouse.ino` (456 lines) for ease of use and traditional Arduino workflow.

## Core Implementation

**Sensor Integration**
- MPU6050: I2C driver for 6-axis IMU (±500°/s gyro, ±4g accel)
- ADXL335: Analog driver for 3-axis accelerometer (12-bit ADC)
- Weighted fusion (30% MPU6050, 70% ADXL335) for enhanced stability
- Auto-calibration with gravity compensation on startup

**Mouse Control**
- BLEMouse: Custom HID report descriptor with 4-byte reports [buttons, x, y, scroll]
- Gyroscope → cursor movement (100Hz update rate)
- Configurable sensitivity and dead zone (0.5 default)

**Gesture Recognition**
- Click detection: Acceleration spike analysis (>2.0g threshold) with directional discrimination
- Scroll detection: Sustained tilt angle (>30°) verified across 5 samples
- Pattern-based temporal analysis using 20-sample circular buffers
- 500ms cooldown prevents double-triggers

## Architecture

Single `ai_mouse.ino` file containing:
- **BLE HID Mouse**: Bluetooth communication
- **MPU6050**: Gyroscope and accelerometer sensor
- **ADXL335**: Analog accelerometer sensor
- **GestureRecognizer**: AI-based pattern detection
- **Main Loop**: Sensor fusion and mouse control

All code in one file for simplicity - no separate .h/.cpp modules needed.

## Pin Configuration

| Sensor | Pin | Protocol |
|--------|-----|----------|
| MPU6050 SDA/SCL | GPIO 8/9 | I2C |
| ADXL335 X/Y/Z | GPIO 0/1/2 | Analog (3.3V) |

## Configuration

All settings are `#define` statements at the top of `ai_mouse.ino`:

```cpp
// Mouse sensitivity
#define MOUSE_SENSITIVITY 0.5
#define MOUSE_DEAD_ZONE 0.5

// Gesture thresholds
#define CLICK_ACCEL_THRESHOLD 2.0
#define SCROLL_TILT_THRESHOLD 30.0
#define GESTURE_COOLDOWN 500
```

## Documentation

- INSTALL.md: Arduino IDE setup, board configuration, pairing workflow
- CIRCUIT.md: Wiring diagrams, PCB layout considerations
- CONFIG.md: Tunable thresholds and sensitivity parameters
- CHANGES.md: Single-file simplification details

## Benefits of Single-File Structure

✅ **Simple** - One file to open and edit  
✅ **Familiar** - Traditional Arduino project structure  
✅ **Easy to share** - Just distribute one file  
✅ **Clear configuration** - All settings at top of file  
✅ **Reduced complexity** - From 11 files (1144 lines) → 1 file (456 lines)

Zero external dependencies beyond ESP32 Arduino core (Wire, BLE).

author: copilot
body:
WiFi scanning returned zero networks due to missing nmcli availability checks, hardcoded interface assumptions (wlan0), race conditions in scan timing, and silent error swallowing. Network status API returned incompatible data structures causing frontend parsing failures.

## Changes

### Phase 1: WiFi Core Fixes
- **Scan reliability**: Auto-detect WiFi interface via `nmcli device`, replace arbitrary 2s sleep with intelligent polling (1s intervals, 10s timeout), deduplicate SSIDs, sort by signal strength
- **Status API**: Return `{wifi: {ssid, interface, state}, interfaces: {...}}` structure matching frontend expectations
- **Disconnect**: Auto-resolve active connection name from interface rather than requiring frontend to pass it
- **Error handling**: Check nmcli availability before all operations, parse and enhance error messages with troubleshooting context

### Phase 2: DASDEC3 Feature Parity
- **Static IP configuration**: DHCP/Static toggle, IP/netmask/gateway forms with validation, apply via `nmcli connection modify`
- **Wired ethernet**: Detect and configure eth0/enpXsY interfaces alongside WiFi
- **DNS management**: Add/remove DNS servers per connection, validation for IPv4/IPv6 addresses
- **Network diagnostics**: Ping, traceroute, DNS lookup, routing table display via subprocess with real-time output
- **Connection profiles**: List, activate, deactivate, delete, toggle auto-connect for all NetworkManager connections
- **Saved networks**: Display WiFi profiles not currently in range, manage auto-connect settings

### Phase 3: Production UX
- **Error messages**: 13 context-aware patterns (e.g., "WiFi disabled" → "Enable WiFi in system settings or run: nmcli radio wifi on")
- **Signal visualization**: Color-coded strength bars (red <25%, orange 25-50%, green 51-75%, teal 76-100%)
- **Input validation**: Reject leading zeros in IP octets (192.168.001.1), WPA2 password length 8-63 chars, RFC 1123 hostname format
- **Tooltips**: Bootstrap tooltips on DHCP, CIDR, gateway, DNS terminology with examples
- **Hostname configuration**: View/set via `hostnamectl` with regex validation at module level (performance)
- **UX polish**: Loading spinners on async ops, session persistence for tab selection, Ctrl+R keyboard shortcut for WiFi scan refresh

## Architecture

Backend API in `hardware_service.py` (NET_ADMIN cap, DBus access) exposes 21 endpoints. Web UI in `webapp/admin/network.py` proxies to hardware-service. Frontend uses Bootstrap tabs for Status|WiFi|Wired|DNS|Diagnostics|Connections organization.

## Security

- Command injection prevented via list arguments (no `shell=True`)
- Input validation: IP addresses (reject leading zeros), DNS servers, hostnames (RFC 1123), passwords (8-63 chars)
- CodeQL scan: 0 vulnerabilities

**DASDEC3 parity:** 10% → 75% (production-ready static IP, DNS, diagnostics)

body:
Implements YouTube music search and replaces bar-chart waveform with sinusoidal wave visualization.

## Backend Changes
- **New `/search` endpoint** using yt-dlp with `default_search: "ytsearch10"`
- Returns structured metadata: title, duration, thumbnail, uploader, video ID

## Frontend Changes

### Search UI
- Search input with dedicated results panel
- Click-to-play from search results
- Safe DOM rendering via `createElement`/`textContent` (XSS prevention)
- Thumbnail URL validation (HTTP/HTTPS only)

### Sinusoidal Waveform
Replaced bar visualization with sine wave generation:

```javascript
// Amplitude-modulated sine wave
for (let i = 0; i < MAX_AMPLITUDES; i++) {
    const sineBase = Math.sin(i * baseFrequency);
    const modulatedAmplitude = amplitude[i] * (height / 2 - 20);
    const y = centerY + sineBase * modulatedAmplitude;
    ctx.lineTo(x, y);
}
```

Two-layer rendering (main + shadow) with gradient fill for visual depth.

## Screenshots

**Search interface with results:**
![Search Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5e3df65-2f22-4b02-8d6f-a25c2afb0eca)

**Sinusoidal wave visualization:**
![Active Waveform](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff8db2db-b937-43e7-91a2-1f3d279c8450)

- CodeQL: 0 alerts
- XSS prevention via DOM methods instead of `innerHTML`
- URL validation on external content

author: jonhenrik13
body:
This pull request improves the startup experience of the application by refactoring how device data is loaded when the UI is initialized. The main change is to move the initial data load into a separate goroutine, which prevents the UI from blocking and ensures a smoother startup for users.

UI startup and responsiveness improvements:

* Removed the synchronous call to `app.LoadDeviceData()` and the immediate redraw of the device list from the main UI thread in `internal/ui/app.go`.
* Added a call to `app.RefreshUI()` in a separate goroutine after the main window is shown to perform the initial data load asynchronously, improving UI responsiveness.

- Add a lightweight TUI toolkit (windows, lists, dialogs) reused by the installer

- Wire up shell commands: install and diskpart
- Add regression tests and comprehensive docs (INSTALLER_GUIDE.md, QUICK_START.md)
- Update build to include new modules and tests

### Impact
- Enables interactive installation wizard and partition management in QEMU; no destructive host-disk writes yet
- Documentation and tests improve verification and onboard users

author: h8d13
body:
This is a follow up to my last [PR#3928](https://github.com/archlinux/archinstall/pull/3928) and original [ISSUE#3599](https://github.com/archlinux/archinstall/issues/3599) 

What we achieve with such a patch:
- Prevent **polluting** the host by having a hacky `running_from_host` definition 
    - Skip `set_kb_layout`  (will be set on target only) via `installer.set_keyboard_language()` and `set_vconsole()`
- This is added to main `__init__.py` to print: EXAMPLE:

```
Fetching Arch Linux package database...
Checking version...
Running from host (H2T Mode)...
```
Or `Running from ISO (Live Mode)`

And will be present in logs to have a trace too (useful if outdated system deps or straight up missing deps). 

**End result:** Makes it so that if you are installing say from a US layout computer and target uses a different layout (ex: laptop), we _do not modify the host system_ and can be built-upon for other host-checks if needed (say for example: extra deps checks or other host isolation related needs).

- Readme clarification Host to target installs without an ISO! 
- Pyright type annotations fixes (was giving me errors but can revert it if needed)

author: gchtr
body:
## Issue

While working with ACF date fields, I figured they were returned as `DateTimeImmutable` objects without a timezone applied when I enabled transforms for all values using the `timber/meta/transform_value` filter.

In the past, I spent a lot of time to figure out how to correctly work with dates and times Timber. I realized that we always have to pass the WordPress timezone when creating DateTime objects, if the date string does not include a timezone string yet. See https://timber.github.io/docs/v2/guides/date-time/#create-a-date-from-a-date-string.

ACF always saves values without a timezone applied, so I think we should pass `wp_timezone()` when creating the DateTime object.

## Solution

Pass `wp_timezone()` when creating the `DateTimeImmutable` object.

## Impact

More robust time handling.

## Usage Changes

None.

## Considerations

None.

## Testing

Updated the tests to make sure that the `DateTimeImmutable` uses the WordPress timezone.

author: copilot
body:
FewShotTransformer initialization failed with `RuntimeError: Given normalized_shape=[25088], expected input with shape [*, 25088], but got input of size[1, 5, 4608]`. LayerNorm was initialized using backbone's reported `final_feat_dim`, but ResNetModel reports 512×7×7=25088 while actually outputting 512×3×3=4608 for 84×84 inputs.

## Changes

**methods/transformer.py**
- Add test forward pass during initialization to determine actual feature dimensions
- Handle dataset-specific input sizes (28×28, 32×32, 84×84) and channels (1 for Omniglot, 3 for RGB)
- Support both flattened (2D) and spatial (4D) backbone outputs

**run_experiments.py**
- Set `flatten=False` when initializing FewShotTransformer (consistent with CTX and other methods)

## Example

```python
# Before: Dimension computed from backbone's final_feat_dim
dim = self.feat_dim  # 25088 for ResNet18

# After: Dimension detected via test forward pass
test_input = torch.randn(1, 3, 84, 84, device=device)
test_output = self.feature.forward(test_input)
dim = test_output.size(1) * test_output.size(2) * test_output.size(3)  # 4608 actual
```

The fix works with any backbone regardless of `flatten` parameter and adds negligible overhead (single 1×C×H×W forward pass during init).

author: andrewbelcher
body:
**Motivation**
<!-- What problem does this solve? Why is it important? What's the context? If this fixes an issue, link to it above. -->
Fixes #187 where `acsf-tools` can choose the technical domain over a custom domain as MEO presents domains in alphabetical order.

**Proposed changes**
<!-- What does this PR change? How does this impact end users? Are manual or automatic updates required? -->
Sort the domains with technical first.

Technically it does this using a check for domain ending with `.acquia-sites.com`. Theoretically you could add a custom domain that ends in `.acquia-sites.com` which would mean the second item in the list would be an `.acquia-sites.com` domain and they _could_ be the wrong way round. But that feels an unliekly edge case that we probably don't need to worry too much about.

**Alternatives considered**
<!-- How else could the original issue / use case be addressed? Why did you choose this solution over any others? -->
Applying this as a filter in `getDomain`, but that feels more complex and affects ACSF where the ordering can be controlled to get the desired domain.

**Testing steps**
<!-- How can we replicate the issue and verify that this PR fixes it? -->
Use this against an MEO site with custom domains. As the domains are sorted alphabetically, add a domain will be sorted before the site name, e.g. `a.example.com` will be before `mysite`'s technical domain.

body:
Changes related to CPU load checking in `korp-install-corpora.sh`:

1. If the CPU load exceeds the load limit, always wait for only one minute before checking the load the next time. (Previously, a heuristic was used that often waited for much longer if the load was high.)

3. Check that the load limit specified as the argument of `--load-limit` is a positive integer; if not, exit with an error.

author: sameryaserr
body:
## Description

This PR implements a secure single-device logout flow as requested in **#25**.
It invalidates only the refresh token used for the current authenticated session — ensuring other active sessions remain unaffected.

## Implemented Features

### Logout (`POST /auth/logout`)

* Refresh token extracted from cookie or request body
* Deletes the corresponding token record from the `Refresh_Tokens` table
* Clears HttpOnly refresh cookie in the response
* Returns `200 OK`

## Behavior & Security

* The invalidated refresh token can no longer be used to issue new access tokens
* Logout affects **only the current device/session**
* No impact on other active sessions
* Ensures proper session termination even if multiple sessions exist

## Highlights

* Safe logout without deleting user account or credentials
* Proper error handling for missing/invalid refresh tokens
* Strict token invalidation ensures improved session security

## Acceptance Criteria

* Access to protected routes blocked after logout → returns `401 Unauthorized`
* Logout call always responds with `200 OK` when successful
* Current session is securely terminated on client + server

## Issue Reference

* Closes #25

def _check_formatting_rules(self, answer: str) -> list[str]:
    """형식 규칙 검증 (formatting_rules)."""
    violations = []

    # 목록형 답변 감지 (숫자 불릿 또는 기호 불릿)
    has_numbered_bullets = bool(re.search(r"^\d+\.\s", answer, re.MULTILINE))
    has_symbol_bullets = bool(re.search(r"^[-*•]\s", answer, re.MULTILINE))

    if has_numbered_bullets or has_symbol_bullets:
        # Phase 4: 서술어 반복 검증 추가
        violations.extend(self._check_predicate_repetition(answer))
        
        # 불릿 간격 일관성만 검사 (문단 구분은 선택)
        if has_symbol_bullets:
            dash_bullets = re.findall(r"^-\s", answer, re.MULTILINE)
            star_bullets = re.findall(r"^\*\s", answer, re.MULTILINE)
            if dash_bullets and star_bullets:
                violations.append("불릿 표시 일관성 필요 (- 또는 * 중 하나만 사용)")

    return violations

The "Search Users" modal caused infinite loading due to a non-existent search endpoint. Searching users by username doesn't align with the device key authentication system where users exchange keys directly.

## Changes

**Replaced SearchUsersModal with AddUserModal**
- Direct device key entry (CW-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX format) instead of search
- Auto-formatting with real-time validation using regex `DEVICE_KEY_PATTERN`
- Validates against adding self or existing contacts (using `contact.id` which contains device keys)
- Socket-based connection requests with proper state management (sending, waiting, error, not-found)

**Updated MainChatLayout**
- Wired AddUserModal with contact list for duplicate detection
- Fixed contact identification to use `contact.id` (device keys) instead of usernames

## Implementation

```tsx
// Auto-format input: "A7X9K3M2P5N8" → "CW-A7X9-K3M2-P5N8"
const handleInputChange = (value: string) => {
  const parts = value.toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9-]/g, '').replace('CW-', '').split('-').join('')
  let formatted = 'CW-'
  for (let i = 0; i < parts.length && i < MAX_KEY_ALPHANUMERIC_CHARS; i++) {
    if (i > 0 && i % 4 === 0) formatted += '-'
    formatted += parts[i]
  }
  setUserKey(formatted)
}

# Fix User Discovery - Add by ID Instead of Search

## Current Problems (See Screenshot)
![image2](image2)

Instead of "Search Users", it should be **"Add User by Key"** - user enters the EXACT key of the person they want to chat with. No searching, just direct connection.

## Description of changes

Certificates expiring within 30 days are now automatically detected and recreated. Previously, only missing domain names triggered certificate regeneration.

**Implementation**:
- Added `IsCertificateExpiringSoon()` to check expiration using a 30-day threshold
- Modified `DeleteExistingCertificateWhenUpdateIsRequired()` to evaluate both domain support and expiration
- Enhanced debug logging to indicate the specific reason for certificate recreation (domain mismatch vs. expiration)

**Behavior**:
When Leap starts, it loads the existing certificate from `LeapCertificatesDirectory`. If the certificate expires within 30 days OR lacks required domain names, it's deleted and recreated with fresh validity. This prevents runtime certificate errors during local development.

body:
**Description**
Implements end-to-end Moodle integration to detect lecture/homework/solution requests, match the correct course (including abbreviations), locate the exact file by type and number, and return a direct, URL-safe PDF link.

**What**
Added intent detection via regex with priority ordering (solution > homework > lecture) and numeric extraction. Course matching uses fullname + shortname with normalization (e.g., "entreprise" → "enterprise") to handle variants. File selection requires exact type+number in module names to avoid wrong-file returns. Moodle API calls fetch enrolled courses, course contents, and matching resources, then append token + forcedownload and follow redirects for direct PDF URLs. All returned URLs are percent-encoded to handle spaces and special characters.

**Why**
No Moodle support existed. Users needed to ask "lecture/homework/solution X from [course]" and get the right PDF, even with course-name variations and filenames containing spaces or special characters.

**How**
Built a detection layer to parse user intent and extract file type + number. Implemented course matching with string normalization for flexible name handling. Connected to Moodle REST API to fetch user courses, locate resources, and resolve direct download URLs with proper encoding to prevent client-side parsing failures.

**Testing**
Manual requests across multiple courses (e.g., algebra, software enterprise/swent) for lecture/homework/solution 1/2; verified correct file is returned and no URL-format errors.

author: lentinj
body:
Whilst looking at the redfish model, it became obvious the existing ``interim_value`` option is somewhat silly:

* It's applied across all fleets, when it should be balancing the effects of each fleet's landings
* It's specified in the quota units (read: harvest_rate), when landings units (read: biomass) would be easier to work with
* It obeys quota.prop / cons.step, which could prevent you from managing to balance the results.

The following rips out the ``interim_value`` option from ``g3_quota()``, and instead adds the following to ``g3a_predate_catchability_project``:

```r
g3a_predate_catchability_project <- function (
    interim_f = g3_parameterized("quota.interim", value = 0,
        by_predator = TRUE, by_step = TRUE),
    interim_unit = unit, . . .)
```

So by default there will be per-fleet, per-step parameters for the interim period, which will be in biomass (assuming that's what the landings data uses). Some of the parameters won't get used, depending on how big the interim period is, but I'm assuming that'll be obvious.

If there's a multi-year interim period, then you'd need to customise ``interim_f`` with ``by_year = 2025:2027``, or whatever makes sense.

``g3_quota()`` also gets ``init_val`` / ``run_historical`` options in place of ``interim_value``, which would make it easier to run quotas in historical periods if that was required at some point.

@willbutler42 any comments? Does this look like it'd work for you? Of course being automatic would be ideal, but I'm still not sure that'd work out.

body:
## Summary

Added a "Shared Favorites" calendar view that shows concerts favorited by both the current user AND all selected friends (intersection logic). Also fixed friend overlay functionality in the "My Favorites" view to properly respect checkbox selection state.

## Changes Made

### 1. Added "Shared Favorites" View

- **New view option**: Added `'shared'` to `CalendarView` type union (`'by-stage' | 'favorites' | 'shared'`)
- **Friend selection UI**: Added checkbox interface allowing users to select one or multiple friends to compare favorites with
- **Intersection logic**: Implemented `getSharedFavorites()` function that returns concerts favorited by BOTH:
  - The current user (required)
  - ALL selected friends (required - must be favorited by every selected friend)
- **Calendar rendering**: Full calendar view showing only shared concerts with:
  - Overlap detection for side-by-side display of concurrent concerts
  - Friend indicators showing all friends who favorited each concert
  - Favorite toggle functionality
  - Concert info popups on click

### 2. Fixed "My Favorites" View Friend Overlay

**Problem**: When unchecking all friends in the overlay, concerts still displayed with multiple colors instead of showing only the user's favorites in a single color.

**Root Causes**:
1. Concert collection logic included ALL friends' favorites regardless of checkbox state
2. Multi-color rendering used ALL friends who favorited concerts, ignoring selection

**Fixes**:
- Modified concert collection (lines 513-518) to only include friends selected in checkboxes
- Updated `getUsersWhoFavorited()` to filter friends by `selectedFriendUsernames` (line 302)

**Result**: Now when all friends are unchecked, only user's favorites show in single color. When friends are checked, their overlays appear correctly.

### 3. Fixed Friend Indicator Consistency

**Problem**: Friend indicators (👥) were inconsistent across views - some showed only selected friends, others showed all friends.

**Solution**: Created two separate functions with clear use cases:

1. **`getAllFriendsWhoFavorited(concertId)`** - Shows ALL friends who favorited a concert
   - Used in: "By Stage" view (line 435), "Shared Favorites" view (line 828), Friends Popup Modal (line 945)
   - Ignores checkbox selection state

2. **`getFriendsWhoFavorited(concertId)`** - Shows only SELECTED friends who favorited a concert
   - Used internally by "My Favorites" view via `getUsersWhoFavorited()`
   - Respects checkbox selection state

**Result**: 
- "By Stage" view always shows all friends (no checkboxes available)
- "My Favorites" view respects overlay checkboxes
- "Shared Favorites" view shows all friends in indicators (helpful to see who else favorited shared concerts)
- Popup modal always shows complete list of all friends

### 4. Fixed Overlapping Concert Layout in Shared View

- Added overlap calculation using `calculateOverlaps(dayConcerts)` (line 680)
- Applied dynamic width and left positioning for side-by-side display (lines 705-718)
- Changed from fixed `w-full` to dynamic percentage-based positioning
- Matches behavior of "My Favorites" view for consistency

## Technical Details

**Files Modified**:
- `frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.tsx`

**Key Functions**:
- `getSharedFavorites()`: Implements intersection logic for shared concerts
- `getAllFriendsWhoFavorited()`: Returns all friends who favorited a concert (ignores selection)
- `getFriendsWhoFavorited()`: Returns selected friends who favorited a concert (respects selection)
- `getUsersWhoFavorited()`: Returns user + selected friends for multi-color rendering

## User Experience

Users can now:
1. **Compare favorites with friends**: Select one or multiple friends to find concerts they all want to see together
2. **Control friend overlays**: Checkbox state correctly affects what's displayed in "My Favorites" view
3. **See comprehensive friend data**: Popup modals show complete list of friends who favorited any concert
4. **View concurrent concerts properly**: Overlapping time slots display side-by-side instead of stacking vertically

## Testing

Tested scenarios:
- ✅ Shared view with one friend selected
- ✅ Shared view with multiple friends selected
- ✅ My Favorites view with all friends unchecked (single color)
- ✅ My Favorites view with friends checked (multi-color overlay)
- ✅ Friend popup modal shows all friends in all views
- ✅ Overlapping concerts display side-by-side in shared view
- ✅ By Stage view continues to show all friends regardless of selection

### Update [urllib3](https://pypi.org/project/urllib3) from **2.4.0** to **2.6.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.6.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`__)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the ``Content-Encoding`` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`__)

.. caution::
  - If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
    your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
    sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
    benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
    `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

  - If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
    respect the changed API of ``urllib3.response.ContentDecoder``.


Features
--------

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in ``HTTPHeaderDict`` using bytes keys. (`3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`__)
- Added host and port information to string representations of ``HTTPConnection``. (`3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`__)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`__)


Removals
--------

- Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers``.
  Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)``. (`3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed redirect handling in ``urllib3.PoolManager`` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool`` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`__)
- Fixed handling of ``SSLKEYLOGFILE`` with expandable variables. (`3700 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3700>`__)


Misc
----

- Changed the ``zstd`` extra to install ``backports.zstd`` instead of ``zstandard`` on Python 3.13 and before. (`3693 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693>`__)
- Improved the performance of content decoding by optimizing ``BytesQueueBuffer`` class. (`3710 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3710>`__)
- Allowed building the urllib3 package with newer setuptools-scm v9.x. (`3652 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652>`__)
- Ensured successful urllib3 builds by setting Hatchling requirement to >= 1.27.0. (`3638 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3638>`__)
   ```

Features
--------

- Added support for version 0.5 of ``hatch-vcs`` (`3612 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3612>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a security issue where restricting the maximum number of followed
  redirects at the ``urllib3.PoolManager`` level via the ``retries`` parameter

- Made the Node.js runtime respect redirect parameters such as ``retries``

- Raised exception for ``HTTPResponse.shutdown`` on a connection already released to the pool. (`3581 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3581>`__)
- Fixed incorrect `CONNECT` statement when using an IPv6 proxy with `connection_from_host`. Previously would not be wrapped in `[]`. (`3615 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3615>`__)

body:
"Heard via" relay links (brown, dashed) were being drawn for all nodes with `hopsAway > 0`, even when formal neighbor data (radio/MQTT) already existed, creating redundant overlapping links.

## Changes

**Core Fix (map/map.html)**
- Track nodes with neighbor data in `nodesWithNeighbors` Set during neighbor link creation
- Skip "heard via" link generation for tracked nodes
- Update comments to clarify behavior

```javascript
// Track nodes with neighbor data (radio or MQTT)
const nodesWithNeighbors = new Set();

// Mark during neighbor processing
if (neighbors.length > 0) {
    nodesWithNeighbors.add(nodeId);
}

// Skip "heard via" for nodes with neighbors
if (nodesWithNeighbors.has(nodeId)) {
    return;
}
```

**Documentation**
- Technical explanation, test cases, and visual comparison diagrams

## Impact

**Before:** Nodes with neighbor data show both green neighbor links AND brown "heard via" links (redundant)  
**After:** Brown "heard via" links only appear for nodes WITHOUT neighbor data

Result: ~33% reduction in link count, cleaner visualization using actual data when available.

## Screenshot

![Before vs After Comparison](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afd91c6e-0ff1-4885-b10d-cae0f2e2d36c)

Left: Nodes B and C have redundant brown links overlapping green neighbor links  
Right: Nodes B and C show only actual neighbor links; brown links reserved for D and E (no neighbor data)

body:
# Security Audit Report

## Automated Checks
Added a GitHub Action (`.github/workflows/security-audit.yml`) to run `govulncheck`. This will flag known vulnerabilities in dependencies automatically.

## Manual Code Review Findings

### 1. VLESS Protocol (`proxy/vless`)
*   **Authentication**: Uses standard UUIDs. The `validator.go` logic zeros out 2 bytes of the UUID (16 bits) for internal processing, reducing effective entropy to 112 bits. This is a known design choice and is considered secure against brute-force attacks.
*   **"Vision" Flow**: Heavy reliance on `unsafe.Pointer` and `reflect` to access private fields in the underlying `tls` and `reality` connections. This is brittle and couples the code tightly to specific internal structures of those packages. While not a direct vulnerability, it increases the risk of stability issues if dependencies change.
*   **DoS Mitigation**: Header parsing in `inbound.go` fallback logic is bounded, preventing infinite loops on malformed input.

### 2. Transport Security (XTLS / REALITY)
*   **REALITY Handshake**: Uses strong primitives (X25519, Ed25519, AES-GCM). Authentication verifies the server's public key signature.
*   **"Spider" Mode**: The client-side crawler uses a simple regex (`href="([/h].*?)"`) to find links. While generally safe due to non-greedy matching, regex parsing of HTML is less robust than a proper parser. The crawler spawns goroutines for each link, which could theoretically be abused if a malicious server returns many links, though `concurrency` limits are applied.
*   **Unsafe Usage**: Similar to VLESS, `reality.go` uses `unsafe` to access `peerCertificates` from the TLS connection.

### 3. SplitHTTP (XHTTP)
*   **Session Exhaustion**: The server (`hub.go`) stores sessions in a `sync.Map` with a 30s timeout for incomplete connections. While this mitigates leaks, a flood of new session requests could still exhaust memory.
*   **Large Uploads**: In `packet-up` mode, the server reads the entire body into memory (`io.ReadAll`) up to `scMaxEachPostBytes`. If this config value is set too high (e.g., hundreds of MBs), it becomes a memory exhaustion vector.
*   **Input Validation**: `x_padding` length is validated.

### 4. Encryption (`common/crypto`)
*   **Nonce Generation**: The `GenerateAEADNonceWithSize` function initializes a nonce to all `0xFF` and then increments. This effectively wraps around to 0 on the first use. As long as keys are unique per session (which they are in VLESS/VMess), this is safe.
*   **Padding**: Uses `crypto/rand` (secure RNG) for padding generation.

## Recommendations
1.  **Monitor "Unsafe" Usage**: The high usage of `unsafe` in protocol handlers is the biggest maintenance risk. Ensure strictly pinned dependency versions.
2.  **Config Limits**: Users should be advised to keep `scMaxEachPostBytes` in SplitHTTP reasonable (e.g., < 16MB) to prevent memory issues.
3.  **Regular Audits**: The added `govulncheck` action will help keep dependencies secure.

---

author: moorec-aws
body:
### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)
Integration tests were not running as part of the release process for the Blender DCC adaptor. This meant releases could be published without validating that the integration tests pass on all supported platforms (Linux, Windows, macOS).

We also want integration tests to run when we merge to mainline

### What was the solution? (How)
Added three integration test jobs to the release_publish.yml workflow:

* LinuxIntegrationTest
* WindowsIntegrationTest
* MacOsIntegrationTest

These jobs run in parallel after the release is tagged and use the reusable integration test workflow from aws-deadline/.github. The PreRelease job now depends on all integration tests passing before proceeding with the release.

Set `integration_tests.yml` to run on push to mainline and added options for running on different branches or tags

### What is the impact of this change?
* Releases will now be blocked if integration tests fail on any platform, ensuring higher quality releases and catching platform-specific issues before they reach production.

### How was this change tested?
This change modifies the CI/CD workflow itself. Testing will occur when the next release is triggered, at which point the integration tests will run automatically as part of the release process.

**Please run the integration tests and paste the results below.**
N/A - This change adds integration tests to the release workflow. The tests will run automatically on the next release.

**If installer/ was modified or a file was added/removed from src/, then update the installer tests and post the test results below.**
N/A - No changes to installer or src files.

### Was this change documented?
N/A - This is a CI/CD workflow change that doesn't affect user-facing functionality or APIs.

### Is this a breaking change?
No.

author: nolbert82
body:
Fixes this error : `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (7) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 0`

`SamplerCustomAdvanced` would crash with “tensor a (N) must match tensor b (M)” when the Scheduled CFG guider received batched timesteps. In that case `timestep` is a tensor of length `batch_size`, but the guider compared it directly to the fixed-length `steps` tensor. 

This change flattens the timestep input to a single scalar preserving dtype/device, and uses `torch.isclose` for the equality check.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [urllib3](https://pypi.org/project/urllib3) from **1.26.15** to **2.6.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.6.1
   ```
   ==================

- Restore previously removed ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` and
  ``HTTPResponse.getheader()`` methods.
  (`3731 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3731>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`__)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the ``Content-Encoding`` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`__)

.. caution::
  - If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
    your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
    sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
    benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
    `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

  - If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
    respect the changed API of ``urllib3.response.ContentDecoder``.


Features
--------

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in ``HTTPHeaderDict`` using bytes keys. (`3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`__)
- Added host and port information to string representations of ``HTTPConnection``. (`3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`__)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`__)


Removals
--------

- Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers``.
  Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)``. (`3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed redirect handling in ``urllib3.PoolManager`` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool`` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`__)
- Fixed handling of ``SSLKEYLOGFILE`` with expandable variables. (`3700 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3700>`__)


Misc
----

- Changed the ``zstd`` extra to install ``backports.zstd`` instead of ``zstandard`` on Python 3.13 and before. (`3693 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693>`__)
- Improved the performance of content decoding by optimizing ``BytesQueueBuffer`` class. (`3710 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3710>`__)
- Allowed building the urllib3 package with newer setuptools-scm v9.x. (`3652 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652>`__)
- Ensured successful urllib3 builds by setting Hatchling requirement to >= 1.27.0. (`3638 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3638>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.5.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for the ``compression.zstd`` module that is new in Python 3.14.
  See `PEP 784 <https://peps.python.org/pep-0784/>`_ for more information. (`#3610 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3610>`__)
- Added support for version 0.5 of ``hatch-vcs`` (`3612 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3612>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a security issue where restricting the maximum number of followed
  redirects at the ``urllib3.PoolManager`` level via the ``retries`` parameter
  did not work.
- Made the Node.js runtime respect redirect parameters such as ``retries``
  and ``redirects``.
- Raised exception for ``HTTPResponse.shutdown`` on a connection already released to the pool. (`3581 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3581>`__)
- Fixed incorrect `CONNECT` statement when using an IPv6 proxy with `connection_from_host`. Previously would not be wrapped in `[]`. (`3615 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3615>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.4.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Applied PEP 639 by specifying the license fields in pyproject.toml. (`3522 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3522>`__)
- Updated exceptions to save and restore more properties during the pickle/serialization process. (`3567 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3567>`__)
- Added ``verify_flags`` option to ``create_urllib3_context`` with a default of ``VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN`` and ``VERIFY_X509_STRICT`` for Python 3.13+. (`3571 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3571>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a bug with partial reads of streaming data in Emscripten. (`3555 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3555>`__)


Misc
----

- Switched to uv for installing development dependecies. (`3550 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3550>`__)
- Removed the ``multiple.intoto.jsonl`` asset from GitHub releases. Attestation of release files since v2.3.0 can be found on PyPI. (`3566 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3566>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.3.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added ``HTTPResponse.shutdown()`` to stop any ongoing or future reads for a specific response. It calls ``shutdown(SHUT_RD)`` on the underlying socket. This feature was `sponsored by LaunchDarkly <https://opencollective.com/urllib3/contributions/815307>`__. (`#2868 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/2868>`__)
- Added support for JavaScript Promise Integration on Emscripten. This enables more efficient WebAssembly
  requests and streaming, and makes it possible to use in Node.js if you launch it as  ``node --experimental-wasm-stack-switching``. (`3400 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3400>`__)
- Added the ``proxy_is_tunneling`` property to ``HTTPConnection`` and ``HTTPSConnection``. (`3285 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3285>`__)
- Added pickling support to ``NewConnectionError`` and ``NameResolutionError``. (`3480 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3480>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed an issue in debug logs where the HTTP version was rendering as "HTTP/11" instead of "HTTP/1.1". (`3489 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3489>`__)


Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Removed support for Python 3.8. (`3492 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3492>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.2.3
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for Python 3.13. (`3473 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3473>`__)

Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed the default encoding of chunked request bodies to be UTF-8 instead of ISO-8859-1.
  All other methods of supplying a request body already use UTF-8 starting in urllib3 v2.0. (`3053 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3053>`__)
- Fixed ResourceWarning on CONNECT with Python < 3.11.4 by backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103472. (`#3252 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3252>`__)
- Adjust tolerance for floating-point comparison on Windows to avoid flakiness in CI (`3413 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3413>`__)

## What this does
<!-- Describe here all changes included in the PR. -->
<!-- If the PR addresses existing issues, here is where you would write "Closes #99999". See https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue -->
Adds a Procedural Story Generator which spawns a ruin which may contain a (living or dead) occupant and some loot. The ruins always contain the following two new machines:

- Planetary Relay which acts as a Telecomms Relay for the entire planet.
- Old Database which generates a research disk and a log of the ruin's occupant's stay on the planet.

To activate the relay and receive the tech disk + story, activate the Old Database and wait 5-15min for it to warm up. The occupant's story is mostly fluff but it may have information about the planet, the planet's climate, the main ruin spawned on the planet, local mobs, and more. Beware - occupants may be infected with diseases!

DNM until #38671 is merged.

## Why it's good
<!-- Explain why you think these changes are good, or otherwise why you wanted to make them and have them merged. -->
The Planetary Relay allows players to communicate with other players on the station while exploring planets. The Old Database provides a slight incentive in exploring by providing research levels. Occupants provide more loot opportunities as well as possible rare antibodies, if they are infected.

## How it was tested
<!-- Document what procedures you used to test this PR here, including any images if helpful. -->
Spawned every ruin type and occupant type. Verified ruins function properly and logs are sane. Verified players on planets can now communicate with the station if their relay is activated. Verified players on the procgen zlevel but not on a planet with an active relay cannot communicate with the station.

body:
Extracts user management from Admin Settings into a dedicated Users navigation page. Managers gain read-only user list access; admins retain full CRUD operations including a new "Add User" modal.

**Updated to integrate with latest API changes from PR #188** - now uses split manager name fields (`manager_first_name`/`manager_last_name`) instead of combined `manager_name`.

## Screenshots

### Users Page (Admin View)
![Users Page Admin View](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50099810-240d-4f85-91cd-a5231c834dc5)

### Add User Modal
![Add User Modal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/222afde4-38e6-4cf2-b078-380220c59850)

### Admin Settings (Users Tab Removed)
![Admin Settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/247733ba-630a-4441-aae7-64334ccdd7cb)

## Changes

- **New UserManagement component** (`frontend/src/components/UserManagement.jsx`)
  - Extracted all user management logic from AdminSettings
  - **Integrated with updated API**: Uses split manager name fields (`manager_first_name`, `manager_last_name`)
  - Role-based UI: managers see read-only table, admins see full controls
  - Added "Add User" modal with fields: email, first/last name, role, password, optional manager (split name fields)
  - Bulk operations (role update, delete) restricted to admins
  - Informational banner for managers explaining read-only access
  - Search functionality properly concatenates split manager name fields

- **Navigation updates** (`frontend/src/App.jsx`)
  - Added "Users" nav item with `Users` icon after Companies
  - Route accessible to both `admin` and `manager` roles
  - Previous admin-only restriction lifted for this page

- **AdminSettings cleanup** (`frontend/src/components/AdminSettings.jsx`)
  - Removed "Users" tab entirely
  - Removed all user-related state, functions, and UI (20+ functions, 400+ lines)
  - Retained Overview, Database, Branding, Security tabs
  - Updated Overview tab with navigation guidance pointing to new Users page

- **Documentation updates**
  - `wiki/Admin-Guide.md`: Updated user management location references
  - `wiki/Features.md`: Added Users page feature, noted manager access
  - `README.md`: Updated admin features section

## Access Control

```javascript
// Managers: read-only view
{user?.role === 'manager' && (
  <Alert>
    <Info className="h-4 w-4" />
    <AlertDescription>
      You have read-only access to user information. Contact an administrator to make changes.
    </AlertDescription>
  </Alert>
)}

// Admins: full controls
{user?.role === 'admin' && (
  <>
    <Button onClick={() => setAddUserDialogOpen(true)}>
      <UserPlus className="h-4 w-4" />
      Add User
    </Button>
    <Select value={u.role} onValueChange={(v) => handleRoleChange(u.id, v)} />
  </>
)}
```

## Add User Implementation

Uses existing `/api/auth/register` endpoint. Admin can specify role during creation, bypassing default "employee" assignment. Form validates email uniqueness, password strength, and required fields before submission. Supports split manager name fields with optional manager information.

## API Integration

Successfully integrated with backend API changes from PR #188:
- User edit modal has separate fields for manager first name and last name
- Search concatenates `manager_first_name` and `manager_last_name` for filtering
- Display logic properly formats split manager names as "First Last"
- Backend maintains backward compatibility with combined `manager_name` format

## Testing

- ✅ All 27 frontend tests passing
- ✅ Frontend build successful
- ✅ Backend integration verified
- ✅ Manual testing confirms all features working with updated API

### Update [asgiref](https://pypi.org/project/asgiref) from **3.7.2** to **3.11.0**.


<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.11.0
   ```
   -------------------

* ``sync_to_async`` gains a ``context`` parameter, similar to those for
  ``asyncio.create_task``, ``TaskGroup`` &co, that can be used on Python 3.11+ to
  control the context used by the underlying task.

  The parent context is already propagated by default but the additional
  control is useful if multiple ``sync_to_async`` calls need to share the same
  context, e.g. when used with ``asyncio.gather()``.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.10.0
   ```
   -------------------

* Added AsyncSingleThreadContext context manager to ensure multiple AsyncToSync
  invocations use the same thread. (511)

   ```
   ------------------

* Adds support for Python 3.14.

* Fixes wsgi.errors file descriptor in WsgiToAsgi adapter.

   ------------------

* Drops support for (end-of-life) Python 3.8.

  function. (471)

* Fixes a reference cycle in Local (508)

* Fixes a deadlock in CurrentThreadExecutor with nested async_to_sync →
  sync_to_async → async_to_sync → create_task calls. (494)

* The ApplicationCommunicator testing utility will now return the task result
  if it's already completed on send_input and receive_nothing. You may need to
  catch (e.g.) the asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError if sending messages to
  already finished consumers in your tests. (505)
   ```

   ```
   ------------------

* Fixes a regression in 3.8.0 affecting nested task cancellation inside
  sync_to_async.
   ```

   ```
   ------------------

* Adds support for Python 3.12.

* Drops support for (end-of-life) Python 3.7.

* Fixes task cancellation propagation to subtasks when using synchronous Django
  middleware.

* Allows nesting ``sync_to_async`` via ``asyncio.wait_for``.

* Corrects WSGI adapter handling of root path.

* Handles case where `"client"` is ``None`` in WsgiToAsgi adapter.
   ```

This PR updates [urllib3](https://pypi.org/project/urllib3) from **1.26.8** to **2.6.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.6.1
   ```
   ==================

- Restore previously removed ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` and
  ``HTTPResponse.getheader()`` methods.
  (`3731 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3731>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`__)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the ``Content-Encoding`` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`__)

.. caution::
  - If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
    your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
    sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
    benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
    `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

  - If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
    respect the changed API of ``urllib3.response.ContentDecoder``.


Features
--------

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in ``HTTPHeaderDict`` using bytes keys. (`3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`__)
- Added host and port information to string representations of ``HTTPConnection``. (`3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`__)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`__)


Removals
--------

- Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers``.
  Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)``. (`3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed redirect handling in ``urllib3.PoolManager`` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool`` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`__)
- Fixed handling of ``SSLKEYLOGFILE`` with expandable variables. (`3700 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3700>`__)


Misc
----

- Changed the ``zstd`` extra to install ``backports.zstd`` instead of ``zstandard`` on Python 3.13 and before. (`3693 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693>`__)
- Improved the performance of content decoding by optimizing ``BytesQueueBuffer`` class. (`3710 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3710>`__)
- Allowed building the urllib3 package with newer setuptools-scm v9.x. (`3652 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652>`__)
- Ensured successful urllib3 builds by setting Hatchling requirement to >= 1.27.0. (`3638 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3638>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.5.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for the ``compression.zstd`` module that is new in Python 3.14.
  See `PEP 784 <https://peps.python.org/pep-0784/>`_ for more information. (`#3610 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3610>`__)
- Added support for version 0.5 of ``hatch-vcs`` (`3612 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3612>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a security issue where restricting the maximum number of followed
  redirects at the ``urllib3.PoolManager`` level via the ``retries`` parameter
  did not work.
- Made the Node.js runtime respect redirect parameters such as ``retries``
  and ``redirects``.
- Raised exception for ``HTTPResponse.shutdown`` on a connection already released to the pool. (`3581 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3581>`__)
- Fixed incorrect `CONNECT` statement when using an IPv6 proxy with `connection_from_host`. Previously would not be wrapped in `[]`. (`3615 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3615>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.4.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Applied PEP 639 by specifying the license fields in pyproject.toml. (`3522 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3522>`__)
- Updated exceptions to save and restore more properties during the pickle/serialization process. (`3567 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3567>`__)
- Added ``verify_flags`` option to ``create_urllib3_context`` with a default of ``VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN`` and ``VERIFY_X509_STRICT`` for Python 3.13+. (`3571 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3571>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a bug with partial reads of streaming data in Emscripten. (`3555 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3555>`__)


Misc
----

- Switched to uv for installing development dependecies. (`3550 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3550>`__)
- Removed the ``multiple.intoto.jsonl`` asset from GitHub releases. Attestation of release files since v2.3.0 can be found on PyPI. (`3566 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3566>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.3.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added ``HTTPResponse.shutdown()`` to stop any ongoing or future reads for a specific response. It calls ``shutdown(SHUT_RD)`` on the underlying socket. This feature was `sponsored by LaunchDarkly <https://opencollective.com/urllib3/contributions/815307>`__. (`#2868 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/2868>`__)
- Added support for JavaScript Promise Integration on Emscripten. This enables more efficient WebAssembly
  requests and streaming, and makes it possible to use in Node.js if you launch it as  ``node --experimental-wasm-stack-switching``. (`3400 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3400>`__)
- Added the ``proxy_is_tunneling`` property to ``HTTPConnection`` and ``HTTPSConnection``. (`3285 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3285>`__)
- Added pickling support to ``NewConnectionError`` and ``NameResolutionError``. (`3480 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3480>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed an issue in debug logs where the HTTP version was rendering as "HTTP/11" instead of "HTTP/1.1". (`3489 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3489>`__)


Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Removed support for Python 3.8. (`3492 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3492>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.2.3
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for Python 3.13. (`3473 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3473>`__)

Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed the default encoding of chunked request bodies to be UTF-8 instead of ISO-8859-1.
  All other methods of supplying a request body already use UTF-8 starting in urllib3 v2.0. (`3053 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3053>`__)
- Fixed ResourceWarning on CONNECT with Python < 3.11.4 by backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103472. (`#3252 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3252>`__)
- Adjust tolerance for floating-point comparison on Windows to avoid flakiness in CI (`3413 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3413>`__)

author: johnburbridge
body:
## Overview

Implements production-ready native image build pipeline with cross-platform support, automated smoke tests, and GitHub release integration. Builds on the successful GraalVM compatibility validation from SPI-921.

## Changes

### 1. Enhanced GraalVM Native Build Configuration (`build.gradle.kts`)

**Dynamic Binary Naming:**
- Platform-aware naming: `cycletime-server-{version}-{platform}`
- Examples:
  - `cycletime-server-0.4.0-macos-aarch64` (Apple Silicon)
  - `cycletime-server-0.4.0-macos-x86_64` (Intel Mac)
  - `cycletime-server-0.4.0-linux-x86_64` (Linux)

**Production-Ready Build Arguments:**
- Runtime initialization fixes (Logback, SLF4J, Kotlin UUID) from SPI-921
- G1 garbage collector for server workloads
- Resource inclusion (application.conf, logback.xml)
- Explicit reflection config reference
- Memory optimization settings
- Compatibility mode for cross-platform builds

**Enhanced Agent Configuration:**
- Metadata collection from unit and integration tests
- Auto-merge with existing reflection configs
- Output to `src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/`

### 2. Cross-Platform CI/CD Workflow (`.github/workflows/native-build.yml`)

**Matrix Build Strategy:**
- macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon) - macos-14 runners
- macOS x86_64 (Intel Mac) - macos-13 runners  
- Linux x86_64 - ubuntu-latest runners
- Windows support deferred for future iteration

**Automated Smoke Tests:**
Each platform validates:
- ✅ Server starts successfully
- ✅ Health endpoint responds
- ✅ MCP endpoint exists and responds
- ✅ Process remains stable

**Artifact Management:**
- Platform-specific binary uploads
- SHA256 checksum generation
- 30-day artifact retention
- Automated GitHub release creation

**Workflow Features:**
- Parallel platform builds (fail-fast: false)
- 45-minute timeout per platform
- GraalVM 21.0.8 with graalvm-community distribution
- Comprehensive validation and reporting

## Performance Benefits

Validated in SPI-921:
- ⚡ **5.3x faster startup**: 2.0s vs 10.7s JVM
- 💾 **72% memory reduction**: 28MB vs 99MB heap
- 📦 **No JVM dependency** required
- 🎯 **Production-optimized** for server workloads

## Testing Strategy

### CI Validation
1. **Build Verification**: All platforms compile successfully
2. **Smoke Tests**: Automated health checks per platform
3. **Artifact Validation**: Binaries uploaded and checksums generated
4. **Release Creation**: Draft release with all binaries

### Local Testing
- Enhanced configuration validated
- Platform detection logic verified
- All SPI-921 findings incorporated

## Acceptance Criteria Status

### Build Configuration ✅
- [x] Configure GraalVM native-image plugin
- [x] Define reflection configuration (auto-generated in SPI-921)
- [x] Configure resource inclusion
- [x] Set up serialization hints
- [x] Define reachability metadata

### Platform Targets (75% Complete)
- [x] macOS ARM (aarch64-darwin)
- [x] macOS Intel (x86_64-darwin)
- [x] Linux x86_64 (x86_64-linux)
- [ ] Windows x86_64 (deferred for future iteration)

### CI/CD Integration ✅
- [x] Add native build jobs to GitHub Actions
- [x] Configure matrix builds for target platforms
- [x] Implement artifact naming convention
- [x] Set up artifact upload for distribution
- [x] Add smoke tests for native executables

### Quality Gates (Pending CI Validation)
- [ ] Native executable starts successfully on all platforms
- [ ] Database initialization works in native mode
- [ ] MCP server responds to requests in native mode
- [ ] Memory usage comparable to JAR execution
- [ ] Startup time < 2 seconds

## Dependencies

- **Builds on**: SPI-921 (GraalVM Compatibility Research) - ✅ Complete
- **Blocks**: SPI-935 (Integration Testing - should test both JAR and native builds)

## Risks and Mitigations

**Risk**: Platform-specific build failures in CI
**Mitigation**: Fail-fast disabled, parallel builds with independent validation

**Risk**: Smoke tests may be flaky
**Mitigation**: Configurable wait periods, health check retries

**Risk**: Binary size may be large
**Mitigation**: Optimization level -Ob balances size and performance (96MB validated in SPI-921)

## Deployment Impact

- Native binaries available as GitHub release artifacts
- Users can download platform-specific executables
- No changes to existing JAR distribution
- Docker images remain unchanged (uses JAR)

## Documentation

Will be added in follow-up:
- Native binary usage guide
- Platform-specific installation instructions
- Performance comparison documentation

## Estimated Points: 13

Reflects:
- GraalVM native-image configuration complexity (4 pts) ✅
- Multi-platform build matrix setup (3 pts) ✅
- Reflection/resource metadata integration (3 pts) ✅
- Platform-specific testing and smoke tests (3 pts) - In Progress

## Related Linear Issue

[SPI-949: Native Build Pipeline (GraalVM)](https://linear.app/spiral-house/issue/SPI-949)
