body:
This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **6.2.5** to **9.0.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.2
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress feature added in pytest 9.0.0 has been disabled by default, except on Windows, due to compatibility issues with some terminal emulators.

  You may enable it again by passing ``-p terminalprogress``. We may enable it by default again once compatibility improves in the future.

  Additionally, when the environment variable ``TERM`` is ``dumb``, the escape codes are no longer emitted, even if the plugin is enabled.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the :confval:`tmp_path_retention_count` settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13946 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13946>`_: The private ``config.inicfg`` attribute was changed in a breaking manner in pytest 9.0.0.
  Due to its usage in the ecosystem, it is now restored to working order using a compatibility shim.
  It will be deprecated in pytest 9.1 and removed in pytest 10.


- `13965 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13965>`_: Fixed quadratic-time behavior when handling ``unittest`` subtests in Python 3.10.



Improved documentation
----------------------

- `4492 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/4492>`_: The API Reference now contains cross-reference-able documentation of :ref:`pytest's command-line flags <command-line-flags>`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.1
   ```
   =========================

Bug fixes
---------

- `13895 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13895>`_: Restore support for skipping tests via ``raise unittest.SkipTest``.


- `13896 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13896>`_: The terminal progress plugin added in pytest 9.0 is now automatically disabled when iTerm2 is detected, it generated desktop notifications instead of the desired functionality.


- `13904 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13904>`_: Fixed the TOML type of the verbosity settings in the API reference from number to string.


- `13910 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13910>`_: Fixed `UserWarning: Do not expect file_or_dir` on some earlier Python 3.12 and 3.13 point versions.



Packaging updates and notes for downstreams
-------------------------------------------

- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.



Contributor-facing changes
--------------------------

- `13891 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13891>`_, `#13942 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13942>`_: The CI/CD part of the release automation is now capable of
  creating GitHub Releases without having a Git checkout on
  disk -- by :user:`bluetech` and :user:`webknjaz`.


- `13933 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13933>`_: The tox configuration has been adjusted to make sure the desired
  version string can be passed into its :ref:`package_env` through
  the ``SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION_FOR_PYTEST`` environment
  variable as a part of the release process -- by :user:`webknjaz`.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table remains supported, but both tables cannot be used at the same time.

  If you prefer to use a separate configuration file, or don't use ``pyproject.toml``, you can use ``pytest.toml`` or ``.pytest.toml``:

  .. code-block:: toml

       pytest.toml or .pytest.toml
      [pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The documentation now (sometimes) shows configuration snippets in both TOML and INI formats, in a tabbed interface.

  See :ref:`config file formats` for full details.


- `13823 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823>`_: Added a **"strict mode"** enabled by the :confval:`strict` configuration option.

  When set to ``true``, the :confval:`strict` option currently enables

  * :confval:`strict_config`
  * :confval:`strict_markers`
  * :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids`
  * :confval:`strict_xfail`

  The individual strictness options can be explicitly set to override the global :confval:`strict` setting.

  The previously-deprecated ``--strict`` command-line flag now enables strict mode.

  If pytest adds new strictness options in the future, they will also be enabled in strict mode.
  Therefore, you should only enable strict mode if you use a pinned/locked version of pytest,
  or if you want to proactively adopt new strictness options as they are added.

  See :ref:`strict mode` for more details.


- `13737 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13737>`_: Added the :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids` configuration option.

  When set, pytest emits an error if it detects non-unique parameter set IDs,
  rather than automatically making the IDs unique by adding `0`, `1`, ... to them.
  This can be particularly useful for catching unintended duplicates.


- `13072 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13072>`_: Added support for displaying test session **progress in the terminal tab** using the `OSC 9;4; <https://conemu.github.io/en/AnsiEscapeCodes.html#ConEmu_specific_OSC>`_ ANSI sequence

body: ### Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filters for noise filtering - Implemented a FIR filter (utama_core/run/refiners/filters.py) - Wrote unit tests to verify that mean squared error is reduced across the board (utama_core/tests/refiners/noise_filter_test.py) - Integrated filters into the position refiners (utama_core/run/refiners/position.py) - Added utilities for exporting vision data and real time tracking of robot coordinates during live testing (utama_core/run/refiners/position.py) -> Moved to testing/data_processing - Modified other unit tests affected by PositionRefiner taking more arguments necessary for the filters (utama_core/tests/refiners/position_unit_test.py and position_refiner_integration_test.py) - Added a folder (vision_data) with various datasets generated from simulations for use in unit testing and running analytics - Analysed the filters to optimise parameters and verify effectiveness in a Jupyter notebook (vision_data/filter_results_summary.ipynb) -> Moved to testing/data_processing - Added multiple dependencies to Pixi: scipy, seaborn, pyqtgraph, pyside6 (pixi.toml) ### Results achieved When testing with grSim using the PID controller under random noise with standard deviation of 10 cm, we achieved a 45% improvement in robot positioning accuracy. However, under the DWA controller, it creates random oscillations. We suspect it is due to the phase delay that FIR filters inherently caused. As such, we have since focused on developing a Kalman filter. ### Note: Kindly keep the additional unused parameters to the Position Refiner. It is required for Kalman filters, and removing it will require double work. Completed by @szeyoong-low and @JiamingLiu5

author: copilot
body:
Adds a self-contained marketing director AI agent system with campaign generation, ROI analysis, and budget optimization capabilities.

## Components

**`agent_core.py`** (479 lines)
- Market position analysis and strategic planning
- Interactive chat interface with context-aware responses
- KPI definition and timeline generation

**`campaign_generator.py`** (936 lines)
- Multi-channel campaign generation (email, social, paid ads, content, events)
- Audience segmentation with persona generation
- Content calendar and creative brief creation
- Budget allocation across channels

**`roi_calculator.py`** (1,044 lines)
- ROI/ROAS calculations with CAC/LTV analysis
- Budget optimization using historical performance data
- Predictive ROI with confidence intervals
- Channel performance benchmarking

**`marketing_director_demo.py`** (553 lines)
- Interactive CLI with 8 demonstration modes
- End-to-end workflow examples

## Implementation Details

All division operations use safe helpers to prevent ZeroDivisionError:

```python
@staticmethod
def _safe_divide(numerator: float, denominator: float, default: float = 0) -> float:
    """Safely perform division, returning default if denominator is zero."""
    return numerator / denominator if denominator != 0 else default
```

Constants defined for magic numbers:
```python
DEFAULT_ROI_PERCENTAGE = 100
DEFAULT_LTV_PERIOD_MONTHS = 36  # Assumed customer lifetime period
```

No external dependencies—uses only Python stdlib.

## Usage

```python
from marketing_director_agent import (
    MarketingDirectorAgent,
    CampaignGenerator,
    ROICalculator
)

# Generate campaign
generator = CampaignGenerator()
campaign = generator.generate_campaign(
    campaign_name='Q1 Lead Gen',
    objective='lead_generation',
    target_audience={'industry': 'Technology'},
    budget=50000,
    duration_days=60
)

# Calculate ROI
calculator = ROICalculator()
roi = calculator.calculate_campaign_roi(
    campaign_data={'total_budget': 50000},
    results_data={'revenue': 200000, 'leads': 800, 'customers': 120}
)

# Optimize budget
optimization = calculator.optimize_budget_allocation(
    total_budget=100000,
    channels=['email', 'social_media', 'paid_ads'],
    historical_performance=past_data
)
```

Interactive demo: `python marketing-director-agent/marketing_director_demo.py`

body:
# 🧾 Pull Request – Actualización Mayor del Integrador (Flujo Unificado + Reportes + Trazabilidad + Cierre Automático)

## 🚀 Resumen
Este PR introduce una actualización mayor al integrador, unificando el flujo manual y automático, robusteciendo el manejo de resultados HL7, agregando trazabilidad avanzada y habilitando nuevos reportes de pendientes/enviados, junto con el cierre automático de exámenes.  
La aplicación ahora es más estable, más auditable y más profesional.

---

## ✨ Cambios principales

### 🔧 1. Unificación del flujo manual y automático
- Ambos flujos (GUI y automático) ahora comparten la misma lógica central de envío.
- Gestión uniforme de estados: `PENDING`, `SENT`, `ERROR`, `MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`.
- Consolida validaciones y elimina duplicación de lógica.

---

### 🧠 2. Implementación del cierre automático del examen
- Si al menos *un analito* se envía correctamente, se ejecuta automáticamente `actualizar_examenlab_fecha`.
- Se replica la lógica del flujo manual con trazabilidad consistente.
- Agregado manejo de errores y logging detallado.

---

### 📊 3. Nuevo módulo de reportes
#### Reporte de Pendientes
- Muestra analitos aún no enviados.
- Identifica rápidamente retrasos o fallos.

#### Reporte de Enviados
- Nuevo módulo solicitado por requerimientos operativos.
- Permite ver qué se envió, cuándo y con qué respuesta.
- Incluye filtros por fecha, paciente, analizador, estado y tipo de envío.

---

### 🔍 4. Nuevo módulo de trazabilidad completa
Incluye:
- HL7 RAW original  
- OBX generados  
- Requests y Responses del API  
- Timeline completo por examen  
- Estados individuales por analito  

Ideal para soporte técnico y auditorías.

---

### 🗄️ 5. Actualizaciones en la base de datos (SQLite)
- Nuevos campos de auditoría en `hl7_results` y `hl7_obx_results`.
- Guardado completo de requests, responses, errores y timestamps.
- Facilita reportes avanzados y reconstrucción exacta del flujo.

---

### 🛠️ 6. Nuevos helpers y validaciones
- Helper para evaluar si al menos un analito fue enviado correctamente.
- Helper para obtener `paciente_doc` desde `id_examen`.
- Limpieza de valores inválidos provenientes del HL7 (`^^`, vacíos, inconsistentes).
- Mayor robustez en búsquedas y reenvíos.

---

### 🖥️ 7. Mejoras en UI (Monitor)
- Nuevos tabs SQLA, Reports, Traceability.
- Interfaz más clara en Orders & Results.
- Presentación simplificada por examen (una fila por examen).
- Doble clic para ver OBX detallado.
- Indicadores visuales para estados OK / ERROR / PENDING.

---

### 📚 8. README completamente actualizado
Incluye:
- Documentación de arquitectura  
- Flujo manual y automático  
- Modelo de datos  
- Instalación paso a paso  
- Descripción de cada módulo  
- Roadmap  

---

## 🧪 Pruebas realizadas
- Ingesta y parsing de HL7 Finecare con diferentes estructuras.
- Envío automático → verificación de cierre automático.
- Envío manual → flujo consistente.
- Validación de mapping.json y hl7_map.yaml.
- Trazabilidad completa validada en UI.
- Manejo de errores por analito y por examen.
- Pruebas con API real (Sofia/SNT).

---

## 🧱 Impacto
- La arquitectura queda unificada y lista para nuevas extensiones.
- Se reduce el riesgo de errores silenciosos.
- El sistema ahora es completamente auditable.
- Se habilita monitoreo operativo real para laboratorio/cliente.

---

Implemented Vercel Web Analytics for plain HTML site

Project Analysis:
- This is a plain HTML site (rangestanhome) with a single index.html file
- No package.json or npm dependencies detected
- Therefore, no package installation was needed

Changes Made:

Modified:
- index.html: Added Vercel Web Analytics script tags to the <head> section

Implementation Details:

For plain HTML sites, Vercel Web Analytics is implemented by adding two script tags directly to the HTML:
1. A script that initializes the `window.va` function and creates a queue for tracking calls
2. A deferred script that loads the Vercel analytics tracking script from /_vercel/insights/script.js

The scripts were added in the <head> section after the existing styles and before the closing </head> tag. This placement ensures:
- The window.va object is defined early in the page load
- The analytics script loads asynchronously with the defer attribute, non-blocking the page rendering
- The implementation follows Vercel's official guidelines for static HTML sites

Why this approach:
- This is a plain HTML site without npm/package managers
- According to the instructions, plain HTML sites should use the direct script tag approach (no @vercel/analytics package needed)
- No framework dependencies to manage
- The implementation is minimal and non-intrusive, preserving all existing code

The changes preserve all existing functionality and only add the necessary Vercel Web Analytics integration. The site will now track user interactions and performance metrics through Vercel's analytics platform.

author: prvshkmr
body:
### Summary
This PR fixes issue #6598, where pressing **Enter** inside the language selector modal causes the modal to get stuck on an endless loading spinner.

### Root Cause
For logged-in users, the language selector loads a `<form>` inside the `select_language_list` Turbo Frame.  
Pressing Enter triggers an **unintended form submission**, but the server response is **not Turbo-frame compatible**, so Turbo cannot replace the frame content.

As a result:
- the Turbo Frame stays in the "loading" state,
- reopening the modal shows the spinner forever,
- only a full page refresh restores normal behavior.

Logged-out users do not see this bug because their modal contains no form.

### Fix
This change prevents the Enter key from causing a form submission inside the language selector modal.  
Avoiding the submission ensures the Turbo Frame continues to behave normally and reloads the language list as intended.

### Testing
- Reproduced issue locally using Docker environment.
- Verified that the spinner freeze no longer occurs when pressing Enter.
- Confirmed that both logged-in and logged-out behaviors remain correct.
- No regressions observed in language selection or modal behavior.

### Additional Notes
- Change follows project coding standards (ESLint for JS).
- Commit history is clean and scoped to the fix.
- Does not modify any localization files except `en.yml` if necessary (none needed here).

## Description

Projects which were deployed before stacks were introduced, were
deployed with the implicit stack name "beta", but this stack name was
excluded from the delegate subdomain. Now that stacks are explicit,
we want them to appear in the delegate, but we need to preserve

body:
PostHog is evaluated locally now, no need for `_cached` ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Refactor** * Updated LLM prompt configuration lookups to fetch fresh configurations on each access instead of using cached versions, ensuring current settings are always applied. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Replaces cached retrieval methods with non-cached ones in `get_llm_config_by_prompt_type()` to ensure fresh LLM configuration and payload data. > > - **Behavior**: > - Replaces `get_value_cached` with `get_value` in `get_llm_config_by_prompt_type()` to ensure fresh LLM configuration values. > - Replaces `get_payload_cached` with `get_payload` in `get_llm_config_by_prompt_type()` to ensure fresh payload data. > - **Logging**: > - No changes to logging behavior, warnings and errors remain the same. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=Skyvern-AI%2Fskyvern&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for f98e6af2ac13f99c2840312a4217fdc27991441f. You can [customize](https://app.ellipsis.dev/Skyvern-AI/settings/summaries) this summary. It will automatically update as commits are pushed. ---- --- 🔄 This PR removes cached method calls from LLM configuration retrieval, switching from `get_value_cached` and `get_payload_cached` to their non-cached counterparts. The change ensures that PostHog experiment configurations are always fetched fresh since PostHog is now evaluated locally.
🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **LLM Configuration Retrieval**: Replaced `get_value_cached()` with `get_value()` for fetching LLM experiment values - **Payload Fetching**: Replaced `get_payload_cached()` with `get_payload()` for retrieving experiment payloads - **Function Scope**: Changes affect `get_llm_config_by_prompt_type()` in `llm_prompt_config.py` ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App as Application participant EP as EXPERIMENTATION_PROVIDER participant PH as PostHog (Local) App->>EP: get_value() [was get_value_cached()] EP->>PH: Fetch fresh experiment value PH-->>EP: Return current value EP-->>App: Return experiment result App->>EP: get_payload() [was get_payload_cached()] EP->>PH: Fetch fresh payload PH-->>EP: Return current payload EP-->>App: Return payload data ``` ### Impact - **Configuration Freshness**: Ensures LLM configurations always reflect the latest PostHog experiment settings without relying on potentially stale cached data - **Local Evaluation**: Aligns with the architectural change where PostHog is now evaluated locally, eliminating the need for caching optimization - **Behavioral Consistency**: Guarantees that configuration changes in PostHog experiments are immediately reflected across all sessions

This pull request adds support for Prisma database migrations to the Docker setup generated by the project, improving the developer experience for projects using Prisma as their ORM. The main changes introduce a new `migrate` service in the Docker Compose configuration, a dedicated `Dockerfile.migrate` for running migrations, and ensure relevant environment variables are set for Prisma commands. There are also minor cleanups to the health endpoint and Dockerfile environment handling.

**Prisma Migration Support:**

* Added logic in `src/index.ts` to generate a `migrate` service in `docker-compose.yml` when Prisma is selected as the ORM, including proper environment variable handling for database connections. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a2a171449d862fe29692ce031981047d7ab755ae7f84c707aef80701b3ea0c80R831-R850) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a2a171449d862fe29692ce031981047d7ab755ae7f84c707aef80701b3ea0c80R738) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-594025fe0a5e19969b4711e5b48a42db78e2a140a75c41432c947abc312f5d40R20-R21)
* Added code in `src/index.ts` to copy a new `Dockerfile.migrate` template to the project when Prisma and a database are selected, and updated the output message to indicate its presence.
* Created `src/templates/docker/Dockerfile.migrate` to install Prisma dependencies and run `prisma migrate deploy` for database migrations.

**Dockerfile Improvements:**

* Updated `src/templates/docker/Dockerfile` to provide a dummy `DATABASE_URL` for the Prisma generate step, ensuring schema generation works without a real database connection.

**Health Endpoint Cleanup:**

* Removed unused project and feature information from the health check endpoint in `src/index.ts` for a cleaner response.

This PR updates [urllib3](https://pypi.org/project/urllib3) from **1.24.2** to **2.6.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.6.1
   ```
   ==================

- Restore previously removed ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` and
  ``HTTPResponse.getheader()`` methods.
  (`3731 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3731>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.6.0
   ```
   ==================

Security
--------

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`__)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the ``Content-Encoding`` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`__)

.. caution::
  - If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
    your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
    sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
    benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
    `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

  - If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
    respect the changed API of ``urllib3.response.ContentDecoder``.


Features
--------

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in ``HTTPHeaderDict`` using bytes keys. (`3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`__)
- Added host and port information to string representations of ``HTTPConnection``. (`3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`__)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`__)


Removals
--------

- Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheaders()`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers``.
  Removed the ``HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)`` method in favor of ``HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)``. (`3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed redirect handling in ``urllib3.PoolManager`` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`__)
- Fixed ``HTTPConnectionPool`` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`__)
- Fixed handling of ``SSLKEYLOGFILE`` with expandable variables. (`3700 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3700>`__)


Misc
----

- Changed the ``zstd`` extra to install ``backports.zstd`` instead of ``zstandard`` on Python 3.13 and before. (`3693 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3693>`__)
- Improved the performance of content decoding by optimizing ``BytesQueueBuffer`` class. (`3710 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3710>`__)
- Allowed building the urllib3 package with newer setuptools-scm v9.x. (`3652 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3652>`__)
- Ensured successful urllib3 builds by setting Hatchling requirement to >= 1.27.0. (`3638 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3638>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.5.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for the ``compression.zstd`` module that is new in Python 3.14.
  See `PEP 784 <https://peps.python.org/pep-0784/>`_ for more information. (`#3610 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3610>`__)
- Added support for version 0.5 of ``hatch-vcs`` (`3612 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3612>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a security issue where restricting the maximum number of followed
  redirects at the ``urllib3.PoolManager`` level via the ``retries`` parameter
  did not work.
- Made the Node.js runtime respect redirect parameters such as ``retries``
  and ``redirects``.
- Raised exception for ``HTTPResponse.shutdown`` on a connection already released to the pool. (`3581 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3581>`__)
- Fixed incorrect `CONNECT` statement when using an IPv6 proxy with `connection_from_host`. Previously would not be wrapped in `[]`. (`3615 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3615>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.4.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Applied PEP 639 by specifying the license fields in pyproject.toml. (`3522 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3522>`__)
- Updated exceptions to save and restore more properties during the pickle/serialization process. (`3567 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3567>`__)
- Added ``verify_flags`` option to ``create_urllib3_context`` with a default of ``VERIFY_X509_PARTIAL_CHAIN`` and ``VERIFY_X509_STRICT`` for Python 3.13+. (`3571 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3571>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed a bug with partial reads of streaming data in Emscripten. (`3555 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3555>`__)


Misc
----

- Switched to uv for installing development dependecies. (`3550 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3550>`__)
- Removed the ``multiple.intoto.jsonl`` asset from GitHub releases. Attestation of release files since v2.3.0 can be found on PyPI. (`3566 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3566>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.3.0
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added ``HTTPResponse.shutdown()`` to stop any ongoing or future reads for a specific response. It calls ``shutdown(SHUT_RD)`` on the underlying socket. This feature was `sponsored by LaunchDarkly <https://opencollective.com/urllib3/contributions/815307>`__. (`#2868 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/2868>`__)
- Added support for JavaScript Promise Integration on Emscripten. This enables more efficient WebAssembly
  requests and streaming, and makes it possible to use in Node.js if you launch it as  ``node --experimental-wasm-stack-switching``. (`3400 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3400>`__)
- Added the ``proxy_is_tunneling`` property to ``HTTPConnection`` and ``HTTPSConnection``. (`3285 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3285>`__)
- Added pickling support to ``NewConnectionError`` and ``NameResolutionError``. (`3480 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3480>`__)


Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed an issue in debug logs where the HTTP version was rendering as "HTTP/11" instead of "HTTP/1.1". (`3489 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3489>`__)


Deprecations and Removals
-------------------------

- Removed support for Python 3.8. (`3492 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3492>`__)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.2.3
   ```
   ==================

Features
--------

- Added support for Python 3.13. (`3473 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3473>`__)

Bugfixes
--------

- Fixed the default encoding of chunked request bodies to be UTF-8 instead of ISO-8859-1.
  All other methods of supplying a request body already use UTF-8 starting in urllib3 v2.0. (`3053 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3053>`__)
- Fixed ResourceWarning on CONNECT with Python < 3.11.4 by backporting https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/103472. (`#3252 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3252>`__)
- Adjust tolerance for floating-point comparison on Windows to avoid flakiness in CI (`3413 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3413>`__)

author: copilot
body:
Implements a campaign generator that produces LinkedIn outreach campaigns with multi-message sequences, targeting criteria, and performance metrics.

## API

```python
from campaign_generator import campaign_gen

campaign = campaign_gen.generate_linkedin_outreach_campaign(
    target_persona="bd_director",
    target_count=100
)
```

Returns:
- **messages**: 5-message sequence spaced 3 days apart with subjects, bodies, and personalization fields
- **targeting**: LinkedIn criteria including job titles, industries, seniority levels, company sizes, locations, interests
- **metrics**: Expected conversion rates (connection accepts, opens, responses, demos) and ROI projections
- **campaign_summary**: Timeline, status, and completion estimates

## Implementation

- **`campaign_generator/campaign_gen.py`**: Core module with `generate_linkedin_outreach_campaign()` function
  - 3 persona definitions: `bd_director`, `procurement_officer`, `grant_manager`
  - Message templates tailored per persona with government contracting context
  - Metrics calculation based on LinkedIn benchmark conversion rates (25% connection, 60% open, 8% response)
  - Input validation with descriptive errors

- **`campaign_generator/test_campaign_gen.py`**: 14 tests covering structure validation, all personas, error cases, and metrics calculation

- **`campaign_generator/README.md`**: API documentation with usage examples for all personas

## Example Output Structure

```python
{
    "messages": [
        {
            "sequence_number": 1,
            "subject": "Streamline Your Government Contract Pipeline",
            "body": "Hi {first_name}...",
            "delay_days": 0,
            "personalization_fields": ["{first_name}", "{company}", ...]
        },
        # ... 4 more messages on days 3, 6, 9, 12
    ],
    "targeting": {
        "job_titles": ["Business Development Director", ...],
        "industries": ["Government Contracting", "Defense", ...],
        "target_count": 100
    },
    "metrics": {
        "expected_connection_accepts": 25,
        "expected_responses": 2,
        "estimated_roi": {"expected_pipeline_value": 0}
    }
}
```

This pull request adds a new NASA Image and Video Library search feature, including a search bar in the navigation, search results dropdown, and a dedicated detail page for selected items. It introduces new API integration, React hooks, and components for displaying and sanitizing fetched content. Supporting types and styles are also included.

**New NASA Image and Video Library Search Feature**

- Added a search bar to the navigation bar, enabling users to search the NASA Image and Video Library and view results in a dropdown. Selecting a result navigates to a new detail page for that item. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6731b388d6de46ce27519f5d03509cc5fe32c2c9085ea7e2c03d7d69e1eaccb1R1-R51) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-936bbe8f9287367653b86ba8ebcabd975227f38cf250997938fc413f9583e93dR1-R68) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d7b339515816d921c6beb7fad6ce6fc3c7cbcf97096aa26b8916aaab0bd46599R13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d7b339515816d921c6beb7fad6ce6fc3c7cbcf97096aa26b8916aaab0bd46599R29) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-bee036f0a13878651fb2eb173ef71420e15cd72e46b6e31b63842e85a5c39ea3R1-R59) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-b2f4bde72d5b4481f44466af0999a1b82f97406217f89ca448f59214e9a139dfR1-R40)

**API Integration and Types**

- Created `src/api/nasaImageAndVideoLibrary.api.ts` to handle searching, fetching assets, and metadata from the NASA Image and Video Library API.
- Defined new TypeScript types in `src/types/NasaImageAndVideoLibraryType.ts` for consistent handling of API responses.

**Detail Page and Data Handling**

- Added a new route and page component `SearchItem` for displaying detailed information and images for a selected NASA library item, using a custom React hook for data fetching (`useNasaItem`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7b339515816d921c6beb7fad6ce6fc3c7cbcf97096aa26b8916aaab0bd46599R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d7b339515816d921c6beb7fad6ce6fc3c7cbcf97096aa26b8916aaab0bd46599R29) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-bee036f0a13878651fb2eb173ef71420e15cd72e46b6e31b63842e85a5c39ea3R1-R59) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b2f4bde72d5b4481f44466af0999a1b82f97406217f89ca448f59214e9a139dfR1-R40)

**Content Sanitization and Styling**

- Introduced `SafeHtml` component using `dompurify` to safely render HTML content from the NASA API, with associated CSS for formatting. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R33) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6ba6b1b934b6e313fb66a138e4eb1ac2b2127e477a56b9fd58a2071eeabb58c0R1-R16) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-42e4f8e16b5df2e57d3aff91062c1653054536fa2c3373745b8f22c90597eb44R1-R20)
- Added new CSS modules for styling the search results dropdown and the item detail page. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f4149c2aa29bd07f2239561c74b95c2e9c05b8e4ebc3df2e909104fc6b32fcd2R1-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c71cea6a8ec8f66c8bac1d2aa1c47a714f0e62d7be2387789af318a7533f3195R1-R49)

**Other Minor Improvements**

- Cleaned up unused code in `src/api/nasaEpic.api.ts` and made a minor CSS adjustment to the navigation bar logo. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-da5446f4f23a319820c486cfefc9ac4178cd8c7dea448d510d3426e5ba7063e2L5-L15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4c1e9e86607021b2edac8734989747f5030882ff8bca99b71cb4a25601cf3095R36)

author: derekg1729
body: ## Context Billing was charging $0 for all LLM calls due to missing LiteLLM cost data in streaming responses. Activity dashboard showed zeros because adapter expected wrong response format from LiteLLM and displayed provider costs instead of user charges. ## Change **Billing System:** - Enable LiteLLM streaming cost via `include_cost_in_streaming_usage: true` config - Establish protocol constant `CREDITS_PER_USD = 10_000_000` (1 credit = $0.0000001) - Single source of truth: `src/core/billing/pricing.ts` with `calculateLlmUserCharge()` - Store `response_cost_usd` as user cost (with markup), not provider cost - Fix payment system to use `usdCentsToCredits()` (10M scale vs old 1000 scale) - Remove deprecated `CREDITS_PER_CENT` constant **Activity Dashboard:** - Implement `LiteLlmActivityUsageAdapter` with Zod validation for `/spend/logs` - Join charge receipts (`llm_usage`) with LiteLLM telemetry on `litellm_call_id` - Display user costs (with markup) in activity table, not provider costs - Aggregate logs into daily buckets for tokens/requests charts - Aggregate receipts into daily buckets for spend chart - Extract `json.id` from LiteLLM responses for join correlation - Add `listChargeReceipts()` port method for activity join **Files:** - `src/core/billing/pricing.ts` - Protocol constant, conversion functions - `src/adapters/server/ai/litellm.adapter.ts` - Extract streaming cost + request ID - `src/features/ai/services/completion.ts` - Use shared billing functions - `src/adapters/server/ai/litellm.activity-usage.adapter.ts` - NEW: LiteLLM adapter - `src/app/_facades/ai/activity.server.ts` - Join receipts with telemetry - `platform/infra/services/runtime/configs/litellm.config.yaml` - Enable cost in streaming ## Risk & Impact **User-facing:** - Credits now use 10M scale (1 credit = $0.0000001 vs old $0.001) - Existing balances from old scale incompatible (requires fresh payment) - Activity dashboard now shows actual billed amounts (with markup) - Old activity rows show "—" for cost (pre-fix data won't join) **Operational:** - LiteLLM config requires restart to apply `include_cost_in_streaming_usage` - Pre-call estimates reduced (`DEFAULT_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS: 2048 → 512`) **Modules touched:** billing, payments, activity, LiteLLM adapter, tests ## Rollout / Backout **Rollout:** 1. Merge to staging 2. Restart LiteLLM service to apply config 3. Users must add fresh credits (old balances incompatible with new scale) **Backout:** - Revert PR - Restore LiteLLM config - Existing charge receipts remain (historical data preserved) ## Evidence - CI: All checks pass (typecheck, lint, unit tests, arch) - Manual validation: Verified with real LLM calls - Provider $0.0006261 → User $0.0012522 → 12522 credits in DB - Activity table shows user costs: $0.002065, $0.01281 - Charts display tokens/requests correctly - Test coverage: 14 new tests for pricing, activity adapter, join logic BREAKING CHANGE: Credit scale changed from 1000 to 10_000_000 per USD. Existing balances incompatible.

author: alexrichey
body: Adds the following to PLUTO - Additional FAR values - MIH Areas for Lots - Transit Zones for Lots (two addl fields) Per Matt, all new fields should be at the very end of the file. Explanations are in the commit messages, or comments in the sql. Logic for assignments for MIH Areas and Transit Zones is at the top of those SQL files. I'm running a build now, and will post a link to the output when it finishes. I'll hold off from merging these changes until confirming logic with GIS and checking that their scripts can gracefully handle the changes. How to review? Commits are atomic, and there aren't that many changes. The additional FAR values are straightforward (just continuing an existing pattern) and for MIH Area and Transit Zone there are maps below to visualize the logic and edge cases. # **TODO** - MIH: AR check with Zoning about a threshold. - Transit Zone: - Determine the severity of a mis-assignment - Determine how / Implement something to hold the tz steady. - Double check pct logic with Zoning # MIH Areas # Logic ```sql -- Similar logic to zoning districts: -- calculate how much (total area and percentage) of each lot is covered by MIH areas -- assign the MIH project ID to each tax lot based on which MIH area covers the -- majority of the lot -- a MIH area is only assigned if more than 10% of the lot is covered by the MIH area -- OR more than 50% of the MIH area overlaps with the lot ``` The questionable splits for MIH Areas can be found in the `qaqc_int__mihareas_questionable_assignments` view in my build schema in postgres (`ar_pluto_new_fields_1893`) ## Some Questionable Splits Overall, only 7 Lots are split between multiple MIH areas. Below are some odd cases #### The following BBLs are split fairly evenly between two MIH Areas. BBL: 3037050014 The southern MIH area covers 50.9% of the BBL... however, you can see that that property is in the northern MIH area. **This one might actually be wrong** --- BBL: 1020130029 These are split between an `Option 1 and 2` and `Option 1` area for `One45 Harlem for All`. However, I don't think this one matters - I think these lots are going to be demolished and redrawn into the MIH Areas as part of the `One45 Harlem for All` rezoning. --- BBL: 2042260001 This is just sort of an odd case. This is PELHAM PARKWAY, and not that it matters terribly, but it probably shouldn't be in either MIH Area. However, it meets the threshold for both, with the slight winner being 1776 Eastchester Road - Option 2, which covers 21% of the lot. # Transit Zones ## Logic ```sql -- Transit zone assignment logic: -- Determine whether > 10% of a lot is covered by one of the transit zones ``` Basically all lots have a transit zone, except for ~2k that are either in the water or are large parks. (e.g. Central Park doesn't have a transit zone, understandably) The questionable splits for MIH Areas can be found in the `qaqc_int__transit_zones_questionable_assignments` table. There are ~800 lots split between multiple zones. ## Questionable Splits (that probably don't matter) A walkway in Staten Island: A Park in Queens ## Questionable Splits (that might have implications) There are a number of cases where the Transit Zones lines were just drawn poorly, and there's not much we can do about it. #### BBL = 4125920057 This lot is split 47% left zone / 53% right zone. And if you zoom out and look at it's block, that seems to indicate that our choice is correct. #### BBL = 4036620026 One more for good measure. We assign cases like this correctly, but there are certainly other cases where we don't. We could try to get clever, and in cases where we find ambiguity then give some preference based on the block. We could also introduce manual corrections.

```go
It("should work in a specific version range (1.0.0, 2.0.0) and third-party dependency redis in [8.0.0, ~)", SemVerConstraint(">= 3.2.0"), ComponentSemVerConstraint("redis", ">= 8.0.0") func() {

ginkgo --sem-ver-filter="2.1.1, redis=8.2.0"

#### 1.40.0

We're adopting a new release strategy to minimize dependency bloat in projects that consume Gomega.  It is a limitation of the go mod toolchain that *test* subdependencies of your project's direct dependencies get pulled in as *indirect* dependencies.  In the case of Gomega, this ends up pulling in all of Ginkgo into your `go.mod` even if you are only using Gomega (Gomega uses Ginkgo for its own tests).

Going forward, releases will strip out all tests, tidy up the `go.mod` and then push this stripped down version to a new `master-lite` branch.  These stripped-down versions will receive the `vx.y.z` git tag and will be picked up by the go toolchain.

Please open an issue if this new release process causes unexpected changes for your projects.

This PR introduces the XMLcontroller class, a standalone utility designed to process raw XML strings without relying on heavy external parsing libraries (like lxml or ElementTree).

The controller provides a complete suite of tools to handle XML data presentation and optimization:

Pretty Printing: Converts raw/flat XML into a structured, indented format.

Smart Text Wrapping: Automatically wraps long text content (e.g., descriptions, body text) to adhere to an 80-character width limit for better readability.

Minification: Compresses XML by removing unnecessary whitespace and newlines for efficient storage or transmission.

author: mohammedattia3104
body:
feat: Implement crypto buy feature

This commit introduces a complete feature for buying cryptocurrency, including the data layer, domain logic, and presentation layer.

- **Data Layer:**
  - `BuyRemoteDataSource`: Defines and implements Retrofit-based API calls to CoinGecko for fetching exchange rates (`/simple/price`) and a list of all coins (`/coins/list`).
  - `BuyRepositoryImpl`: Implements the `BuyRepository` by fetching data from the remote source, handling errors, and mapping API responses to domain entities.
  - `BuyMapper`: Converts raw API data into `ExchangeRateEntity` and provides helpers for mapping currency symbols to CoinGecko IDs and listing supported currencies.
  - Added models for API responses (`ExchangeRateResponseModel`, `CoinListItemModel`).
  - Introduced `BuyIsolateWorker` to offload JSON parsing for large responses to a separate isolate, preventing UI jank.

- **Domain Layer:**
  - `BuyRepository`: Defines the contract for fetching exchange rates and coin lists.
  - Entities: Added `ExchangeRateEntity`, `CoinListItemEntity`, and `TransactionEntity` to model the core business objects.
  - Use Cases:
    - `GetExchangeRateUseCase`: Fetches the conversion rate between two currencies.
    - `GetCoinsListUseCase`: Retrieves a list of available cryptocurrencies.
    - `CalculateTransactionUseCase`: Calculates transaction details, including fees, based on either the amount paid or the amount to be received.

- **Presentation Layer (`BuyScreen`):**
  - **UI**: Created a new `BuyScreen` with a clean, component-based structure. It includes:
    - `CurrencyInputField` for entering amounts.
    - `CurrencyDropdown` in a bottom sheet for selecting from a list of fiat or crypto currencies.
    - `SwapCurrenciesButton` to quickly swap "pay" and "receive" currencies.
    - `ExchangeRateDisplay` and `FeeInfoCard` to show transaction details.
  - **State Management**:
    - `BuyCubit`: Manages the state for the `BuyScreen`, handling API calls, calculations, and user interactions like updating amounts, swapping currencies, and changing selected currencies.
    - `BuyState`: Implemented a `freezed` union for representing UI states (initial, loading, loaded, error).

# Pull Request

<!-- Thanks for contributing to ros2_medkit! -->

## Summary

This pull request enhances the operations and configuration endpoints in the ROS2 Medkit Gateway, improving the stability and discoverability of actions, services, and parameters. The changes transition from a namespace-based operation lookup to a more accurate node-specific introspection approach, add timeout handling for service calls, and introduce parameter reset functionality.

Key Changes:
- Added new GET endpoint for listing component operations with schema information
- Changed DELETE configuration behavior from "not supported" (405) to "reset to default" (200)
- Implemented timeout protection for service calls to prevent indefinite hanging
- Improved operation assignment to components using ROS2's node-specific introspection API
- Added stricter compiler warnings (-Wshadow, -Wconversion) with corresponding type conversion fixes

author: chrreiter
body:
## Summary
Fixes the critical storage migration bug and adds startup health checking.

## Changes
- storage.py: Call `migrations.migrate()` instead of assigning the function reference (line 141)
- __init__.py: Add post-load validation of storage structure; log diagnostics; raise `ConfigEntryNotReady` on critical issues
- tests: Add migration path tests with old schema fixtures

## Impact
- Storage migrations now actually run, preventing data corruption
- Bad/corrupt storage is caught at startup with meaningful logs
- Migration tests prevent regressions

## Testing
- All existing tests pass
- New migration tests cover v1 to v2 upgrade path

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Runs real storage migrations to v2 and validates storage on startup with health logging; updates tests and HA stubs accordingly.
> 
> - **Storage**:
>   - Bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` to `2` and persist migrated payloads.
>   - Ensure migrations run via `migrations.migrate(...)`; validate result type; normalize required keys.
>   - Improved error logging/context for corrupted payloads; no overwrite on migration failure.
> - **Init/Setup**:
>   - Validate loaded storage payload (`schema_version`, `items`, `locations`) and log health summary.

body:
Addresses compilation, security hardening, and test server setup for the NonelessLobby Minecraft plugin.

## Security Fixes (CRITICAL)

### Hardcoded Database Credentials Removed
**Before:**
```java
public static String host = "ms2778.gamedata.io";
public static String password = "y77ei7XP";  // Exposed in source
```

**After:**
```java
// Loaded from config.yml
public static String host = "localhost";
public static String password = "changeme";
```

Added `ConfigManager.loadMySQLConfig()` to load credentials from configuration file instead of hardcoding in source.

### MySQL Connector Vulnerability Patched
Updated `mysql-connector-j` from 8.0.33 → 8.2.0 to fix CVE takeover vulnerabilities affecting versions < 8.2.0.

## Build Configuration

- Fixed deprecated dependency: `mysql:mysql-connector-java` → `com.mysql:mysql-connector-j`
- Updated to patched connector version resolving two separate CVEs

## Documentation & Setup

Created automated test server setup:
- `setup-test-server.sh` - One-command server initialization
- `config.yml` - Default secure configuration template
- 7 documentation files covering setup, troubleshooting, and security

## Configuration Management

```yaml
mysql:
  enabled: false          # Disabled by default
  host: localhost
  username: lobby
  password: changeme      # Forces users to set secure credentials
```

Configuration now loads at plugin initialization before database connection.

## Security Verification

- CodeQL: 0 alerts
- Dependency scan: 0 vulnerabilities
- All credentials externalized to configuration files

author: hn770123
body:
年間休日設定の保存に失敗する問題を修正しました。

変更内容:
- annual-holidays.js: upsertメソッドから不要なonConflictパラメータを削除
- annual-holidays.js: エラーメッセージに詳細情報を追加
- schema-updates.sql: RLSポリシーをFOR ALL形式から個別の操作（SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE）に分割
- docs/fix_annual_holidays_rls.sql: RLSポリシー修正用のSQLスクリプトを追加

問題の原因:
1. Supabase JS v2ではupsertメソッドのonConflictパラメータが自動的にユニーク制約を検出するため、明示的な指定が不要
2. RLSポリシーでFOR ALL USING形式を使用した場合、INSERT/UPDATEでWITH CHECK句が明示的に必要

修正により、ユーザーは年間休日設定を正常に保存・更新できるようになります。

author: jandubois
body:
The new ISO will automatically install it from the apkovl during boot but Lima may unintentionally uninstall it while re-installing manually installed packages. We need to make sure iproute2 is listed in `/etc/apk/world`.

Please review while ignoring whitespace; this PR adds an additional `if` condition around a larger code block.

Further changes:
* Detect when /etc/os-release is a symlink and treat it as an upgrade signal
* Keep a copy of limi-init.log from the upgrade in the data volume because a reboot will replace the copy in /var/log

Fixes #9554

This is a duplicate of #9557, which for some reason doesn't want to run DCO again.

author: copilot
body:
The compiler panicked during codegen when users tried to assign function names to variables (`let a = some_function;`). The type checker allowed function types in variable declarations, but LLVM requires function pointers, not function values.

## Changes

- **Added `FunctionNotFirstClass` diagnostic** to report when function types are used in let declarations
- **Added validation in `process_let_declaration`** to reject function types in all three cases:
  - Explicit type annotation without initializer
  - Type inference from initializer  
  - Both explicit type and initializer
- **Added test coverage** for both inference and explicit type annotation cases

## Example

**Before:** ICE with "function is not a basic type" panic

**After:** Clear error message
```zr
fn this_is_a_function() {}

fn main() -> i32 {
    let a = this_is_a_function;  // Error: functions are not first-class values
    return 0;
}
```

Users should use function pointers instead: `let a: *fn() = &this_is_a_function;`

author: jkeenan
body:
This commit is mostly a manual reversion of commit f1cf82e.  Return to a perl_croak in universal.c; adjust regen/warnings.pl as needed; run 'make regen'; get t/op/universal.t passing.  No documentation changes yet.

Add test for undefined unimport method, then refactor repeated code into a subroutine.  Perform a pattern match rather than a string equality test because testing for exact line numbers inside a test program too fragile for maintenance purposes.

Still one porting test failure.

This should be considered a **first draft** of a pull request to implement GH #23623.

I believe I have implemented the "ask" of GH #23623, but there is one test failure in `t/porting/diag.t` I have not yet been able to resolve.  In `t/op/universal.t` I have written tests to match the message emitted by the newly fatalized `import` and `unimport` cases in `universal.c`, but I have not yet been able to get `t/porting/diag.t` to recognize that that exception message is indeed documented in `pod/perldiag.pod`.
```
$ cd t;./perl harness porting/diag.t; cd -
porting/diag.t .. 1839/? # Failed test 2181 - Attempt to call undefined %s method with arguments via package "%s" (Perhaps you forgot to load the package?) at porting/diag.t line 589
#     Message 'Attempt to call undefined %s method with arguments via package "%s" (Perhaps you forgot to load the package?)'
#     from universal.c line 454 is not listed in pod/perldiag.pod
porting/diag.t .. Failed 1/2368 subtests 
```
Suggestions welcome.

I have not yet made any attempt to estimate the impact of this code change on code on CPAN or out in the wild.  If anyone wants to work with me on that, please contact me.

**NOTE:** Other things being equal, I would prefer to see the pull request for goto-partial-fatal, GH #23782, prioritized for review and merging.

Will need a perldelta entry.

@haarg

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.1** to **7.13.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.13.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: coverage.py now supports :file:`.coveragerc.toml` configuration
  files. These files use TOML syntax and take priority over
  :file:`pyproject.toml` but lower priority than :file:`.coveragerc` files.
  Closes `issue 1643`_ thanks to `Olena Yefymenko <pull 1952_>`_.

- Fix: we now include a permanent .pth file which is installed with the code,
  fixing `issue 2084`_.  In 7.12.1b1 this was done incorrectly: it didn't work
  when using the source wheel (``py3-none-any``).  This is now fixed. Thanks,
  `Henry Schreiner <pull 2100_>`_.

- Deprecated: when coverage.py is installed, it creates three command entry
  points: ``coverage``, ``coverage3``, and ``coverage-3.10`` (if installed for
  Python 3.10). The second and third of these are not needed and will
  eventually be removed. They still work for now, but print a message about
  their deprecation.

.. _issue 1643: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1643
.. _pull 1952: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1952
.. _pull 2100: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2100


.. _changes_7-12-1b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.1b1
   ```
   -----------------------------

- Fix: coverage.py now includes a permanent .pth file in the distribution which
  is installed with the code. This fixes `issue 2084`_: failure to patch for
  subprocess measurement when site-packages is not writable.

.. _issue 2084: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2084


.. _changes_7-12-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083
.. _pull 2085: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085
.. _issue 2086: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086
.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090
.. _issue 2091: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091


.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078
.. _nedbat GitHub account: https://github.com/nedbat
.. _coveragepy GitHub organization: https://github.com/coveragepy


.. _changes_7-11-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/cov

body:
Adds ability to selectively disable zircop lints both from command line and within source code.

## Changes

- **CLI flags**: `--allow/-A <lint_name>` to ignore specific lints. Accepts multiple flags and "all" keyword.
- **In-code directives**: 
  - `// zircop-ignore: <lint_name>` for current line
  - `// zircop-ignore-next-line: <lint_name>` for next line
- **Infrastructure**: New `ignore` module parses comment directives, uses `LineLookup` to map diagnostic spans to line numbers, filters with O(1) HashSet lookups.
- **API additions**: `LintDiagnosticKind::name()` returns canonical lint identifier, `LintDiagnostic::kind()` provides accessor.

## Usage

```zirco
fn example() -> i32 {
    let unused = 10; // zircop-ignore: unused_variable
    
    // zircop-ignore-next-line: underscore_variable_used
    let _var = 20;
    
    return 0;
}
```

```bash
# Ignore specific lints
zircop --allow unused_variable --allow unreachable_code file.zr

# Ignore all lints
zircop --allow all file.zr
```

Lint names: `unused_variable`, `underscore_variable_used`, `unreachable_code`, `empty_struct_used`, `assignment_in_condition`, `empty_if_block`, `empty_else_block`, `empty_while_body`, `all`.

body:
Documents architectural decisions for Zone-related data structures (ZoneBounds and CollisionData).

## Structure

**Section 1: ZoneBounds vs CollisionData**
- Comparison table: purpose, data structure, performance characteristics
- ASCII visualization showing outer bounds vs inner obstacles
- MovementValidator example demonstrating fail-fast validation pattern

**Section 2: ZoneBounds Design**
- Rationale for excluding ZoneId property: avoids circular dependency, eliminates redundancy, maintains Single Responsibility
- Inclusive-exclusive range convention `[Min, Max)` enables seamless zone boundaries without gaps/overlaps
- Complete implementation with Contains(), Clamp(), IsNearEdge()

**Section 3: Shared Library Placement**
- Both classes in `Mmo.Shared` for client-side prediction
- MessagePack DTOs with RLE compression for network transfer

**Section 4: Data Distribution Strategy**
- MVP: Static collision data bundled in client
- Future: Hybrid approach with version-based delta updates
- Implementation examples for both patterns

**Section 5: CollisionData Implementation**
- Tile-based `bool[,]` grid (Width × Height × TileSize)
- Bresenham line algorithm for CanMoveTo() collision detection
- O(1) tile lookup, O(n) path validation

**Section 6: Decision Summary**
- Table of 10 key architectural decisions with rationale

## Key Design Decisions

```csharp
// ZoneBounds: No ZoneId property - Zone owns Bounds, not vice versa
public class Zone
{
    public string ZoneId { get; }
    public ZoneBounds Bounds { get; }  // Value object, no identity
}

// Inclusive-exclusive ranges enable seamless zone adjacency
// Zone A: [0, 1000) × [0, 1000)
// Zone B: [1000, 2000) × [0, 1000)  // No gap, no overlap at x=1000
public bool Contains(float x, float y) => 
    x >= MinX && x < MaxX && y >= MinY && y < MaxY;
```

body:
Implements robust model loading for LLM, STT, and TTS with intelligent fallback strategies (4-bit → 8-bit → fp16 → CPU), offline mode detection, and persistent model serving via FastAPI.

## Core Changes

**Model Loading (`src/llm.py`, `src/stt.py`, `src/tts.py`)**
- Added `ensure_model_exists()` helper with HF Hub validation and offline detection
- LLM: Quantization fallback chain with BitsAndBytes diagnostics and lazy native lib checking
- STT: Manual Whisper loading with pipeline fallback, configurable device via `WHISPER_DEVICE`
- TTS: Dia2 pipeline with `use_global=True` attempt for improved voice quality
- All modules: `local_files_only=True` when offline, detailed logging at each fallback stage

**Model Server (`src/model_server.py`)**
- Loads all models once at startup (persistent memory)
- Enhanced `/health` endpoint reports device, loading strategy, and model info
- New endpoints: `/stt` (transcription), `/tts` (synthesis)
- Default port changed: 8001 → 8000
- Thread-safe operations with locks

**Client Functions (`src/model_client.py`)**
- Added `transcribe(audio_path)` and `synthesize(text, output_path)` for STT/TTS
- Updated base URL to port 8000

**Configuration**
```python
# Environment variables (all modules)
LOCAL_MODELS_DIR = os.getenv("LOCAL_MODELS_DIR", "./models")
OFFLOAD_FOLDER = os.getenv("OFFLOAD_FOLDER", "/tmp/transformers_offload")
DEFAULT_HF_HOME = os.getenv("HF_HOME", "/opt/hf_cache")

# TRANSFORMERS_CACHE triggers deprecation warning if HF_HOME not set
```

## Example Usage

```python
# LLM with automatic fallback
from src.llm import OpenSourceLLM
llm = OpenSourceLLM()  # Attempts 4-bit, falls back to 8-bit/fp16/CPU with logging

# Offline mode - fast failure
HF_FORCE_OFFLINE=1 llm = OpenSourceLLM()  
# RuntimeError: Offline mode: model not found locally. Cannot download.

# Model server health
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
{
  "status": "ok",
  "models": {
    "llm": {"device": "cuda:0", "loading_strategy": "4-bit quantized"},
    "stt": {"device": "cpu", "type": "manual"},
    "tts": {"device": "cuda", "type": "pipeline"}
  }
}
```

## Testing
- `test_model_loading.py` - Comprehensive test suite for all model types
- `test_llm_quick.sh` - Quick sanity check one-liner

## Documentation
- `MODEL_LOADING_IMPROVEMENTS.md` - Complete usage guide with env vars, API reference, troubleshooting
- `VERIFICATION_CHECKLIST.md` - Verification commands and requirements checklist

## Notes
- Zero security alerts (CodeQL verified)
- Backward compatible - no changes to public APIs
- BNB native library check moved to lazy evaluation (avoids import-time file I/O)

body:
Built a complete Electron-based desktop application consolidating TrinityCore development tools into a unified interface with 8 feature modules.

## Architecture

**Desktop Framework**
- Electron 28 with React 18/TypeScript for renderer process
- Type-safe IPC bridge via contextBridge with proper isolation
- Vite build system for development and production

**Component Structure**
```typescript
// Example IPC pattern used throughout
// src/renderer/types/electron.d.ts
interface ElectronAPI {
  startWorldServer: (path: string) => Promise<{ success: boolean; message: string }>;
  onWorldServerLog: (callback: (log: string) => void) => void;
}

// src/main/preload.ts
contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electronAPI', {
  startWorldServer: (path) => ipcRenderer.invoke('start-world-server', path),
  onWorldServerLog: (cb) => ipcRenderer.on('world-server-log', (_, log) => cb(log)),
});
```

## Feature Modules

**Server Manager** (`ServerManager.tsx`)
- Process spawning for worldserver/authserver with stdout/stderr streaming
- Real-time log aggregation with search filtering
- Status tracking via IPC events

**Code Editor** (`CodeEditor.tsx`)
- Monaco Editor integration with C++/Lua/SQL language servers
- Pre-built script templates (creature AI, Eluna gossip, SQL schemas)
- File I/O through main process

**Database Tooling** (`DatabaseManager.tsx`)
- Visual table browser for creature_template, quest_template, item_template
- CRUD operations with modal-based editing
- Connection manager for world/characters/auth databases

**Content Creator** (`ContentCreator.tsx`)
- Form-driven generators for NPCs, quests, items, spells
- SQL script generation with clipboard integration
- Preview panel showing generated queries

**AI Assistant** (`AIAssistant.tsx`)
- Log analysis, code generation, debugging help, content balancing
- Simulated AI responses (placeholder for future service integration)

**Testing Tools** (`TestingTools.tsx`)
- Dungeon encounter simulator with group composition
- NPC behavior validation
- Event simulation with performance metrics

**Patch Manager** (`PatchManager.tsx`)
- Interface for .mpq/.patch file management
- DBC file editor framework
- Texture and map editing tools

**User Manager** (`UserManager.tsx`)
- Real-time player monitoring dashboard
- GM command execution with history logging
- Player control actions (kick, ban, teleport)

## Configuration

**TypeScript**
- Dual configs: `tsconfig.json` (bundler resolution for React) and `tsconfig.main.json` (CommonJS for Electron main)
- Strict mode enabled with proper type definitions in `src/renderer/types/`

**Styling**
- Component-scoped CSS following `ComponentName.tsx` / `ComponentName.css` pattern
- Dark theme with consistent design tokens

## Build Output

```
dist/
├── main/           # Compiled Electron main process
│   ├── main.js
│   └── preload.js
└── renderer/       # Bundled React app
    ├── index.html
    └── assets/
```

Run `npm run build` to generate production artifacts, `npm run dev` for hot-reload development.

body:
# Pull Request Description

## Overview
This PR enhances the AWS Athena Query Federation SDK with refactored credential management, improved federated request handling, and new Substrait plan conversion utilities for advanced query pushdown capabilities.

## Key Changes

### 1. Credential Management Refactoring & Enhanced Federation Support
**Refactoring:**
- Consolidated credential management methods from `MetadataHandler` and `RecordHandler` into `FederationRequestHandler` interface
- Promoted `resolveSecrets()`, `resolveWithDefaultCredentials()`, and `getSecret()` to public interface methods
- Added public accessors: `getCachableSecretsManager()` and `getKmsEncryptionProvider()`

**New Functionality:**
- AWS request override configuration support for federated requests:
  - `getRequestOverrideConfig()` - Extracts configuration from federated requests
  - `isRequestFederated()` - Detects federated requests
- Credential provider factory pattern:
  - `getCredentialProvider()` - Creates providers with optional override configuration
  - `createCredentialsProvider()` - Extensible factory method for custom implementations
- Enhanced `CachableSecretsManager` to support `AwsRequestOverrideConfiguration`
- Fixed empty config options handling in `MetadataHandler.makeSpillLocation()`

**Modified Files:**
- `FederationRequestHandler.java`, `MetadataHandler.java`, `RecordHandler.java`, `CachableSecretsManager.java`

### 2. Substrait Plan Conversion Utilities
**New File:** `SubstraitSqlUtils.java`

**Features:**
- Converts Substrait plans (base64) to Calcite SqlNode and Apache Arrow Schema
- Comprehensive type mapping: Boolean, Integer, Float, String, Temporal, Decimal, Array, Map, Struct
- Enables query pushdown capabilities via Apache Calcite intermediate representation

### 3. Comprehensive Test Coverage
**New Test Files:**
- `FederationRequestHandlerTest.java` - 20+ test cases for credential management and federated requests
- `SubstraitSqlUtilsTest.java` - Extensive SQL conversion tests covering logical operators, comparisons, arithmetic, pattern matching, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, HAVING, and error handling

## Breaking Changes
None. All changes are backward compatible.

## Testing
* All existing tests pass
* 20+ new test cases for credential management and federation
* Extensive Substrait conversion tests with parameterized scenarios
* Snowflake Connector with Query Federation tests in Athena production with all TPC-H benchmark queries.



By submitting this pull request, I confirm that you can use, modify, copy, and redistribute this contribution, under the terms of your choice.

author: farzonl
body:
fixes #159438

This patch adds `MatrixElementExpr`, a new AST node for HLSL matrix element and swizzle access (e.g. M._m00, M._11_22_33).

 It introduces a shared `ElementAccessExprBase` used by both matrix and vector swizzle expressions, updates Sema to parse and validate zero-based and one-based accessors, detects duplicates for l-value checks, and emits improved diagnostics. CodeGen is updated to lower scalar and multi-element accesses consistently, and full AST serialization, dumping, and tooling support is included. This implementation reflects the updated [RFC](https://github.com/llvm/wg-hlsl/pull/357/files) for HLSL matrix accessor semantics.

```vue
<UFormField label="Email" orientation="horizontal">

</UFormField>

author: fw-bot
body:
Currently, we register two separate payments for MPF at the same time as we do for the employee's wages.
This is not what we want to do; as both are not paid at the same time. MPF is also handled separately, and paid outside of Odoo on the government platform, making the registration of separate payments more complex for not many benefits.
Thus, we make these accounts un-reconcilable by default, and will expect accountants to reconcile the statement with the account directly.

body:
Self-steepening (shock term) was causing pulse steepening on the leading edge instead of the trailing edge due to incorrect derivative operator sign.

## Root Cause

The derivative operator used `-im * omega` based on a misunderstanding that FFT convention affects derivative signs. The Fourier derivative identity ∂/∂t → +iω holds regardless of FFT convention:

```julia
# Integration by parts proof:
ℱ[∂f/∂t] = ∫ (∂f/∂t) exp(-iωt) dt
          = +iω · ℱ[f]
```

## Changes

**src/nonlinearity.jl** - Fixed derivative sign in 4 functions:

```julia
# Before (incorrect):
It_w = ifft_plan * It
@. It_w *= (-im * omega)  # Wrong: assumed FFT convention inverts sign
dI_dt = fft_plan * It_w

# After (correct):
It_w = ifft_plan * It
@. It_w *= (im * omega)   # Correct: derivative operator is +iω always
dI_dt = fft_plan * It_w
```

Applied to:
- `nonlinear_operator_kerr_shock`
- `nonlinear_operator_kerr_raman_shock` 
- `nonlinear_freq_gamma_kerr_shock`
- `nonlinear_freq_gamma_kerr_raman_shock`

## Verification

- **Raman response transform**: Verified `fftshift` usage is correct
- **Grid omega convention**: Verified FFT order matching is correct
- **FFT convention**: Verified internal consistency throughout codebase

## Impact

Simulations with `shock=true` now produce physically correct self-steepening:
- Trailing edge steepening (was: leading edge)
- Correct supercontinuum generation dynamics
- Proper soliton fission asymmetry

## Documentation

- `FFT_CONVENTION_ANALYSIS.md` - Technical analysis with mathematical proofs
- `CORRECTIONS_SUMMARY.md` - Executive summary
- `FFT_FIX_README.md` - User guide
- Validation tests: `test_self_steepening_direction.jl`, `test_raman_frequency_shift.jl`
- Interactive verification: `verify_fix_analytical.jl` (runs without dependencies)

body:
## Description
This PR implements the core Runner Service for CloudPulse and refactors the existing API to support persistent storage via DynamoDB. This enables the system to be deployed to a real cloud environment (AWS) where targets are monitored by a distributed Lambda function, decoupled from the API.

## Key Changes
### New Runner Service (apps/runner)
- Implemented a Go Lambda function that runs on a schedule.
- Fetches targets from DynamoDB, performs HTTP probes, and stores results.
- Includes a Dockerfile for building the Lambda container image.

### Shared Library Refactor (internal/)
- internal/model: Centralized Target and Result structs. Added dynamodbav tags to fix case-sensitivity issues with DynamoDB.
- internal/store: Created a Store interface and a DynamoDBStore implementation using the AWS SDK v2.
- internal/probe: Abstracted the HTTP probe logic into a reusable package.

### API Updates (apps/api)
- Refactored main.go and handlers to use the new internal/ shared packages.
- Added support for dynamic store switching:
  - Uses InMemoryStore if table env vars are missing (Local Dev).
  - Uses DynamoDBStore if table env vars are present (Cloud).
    - Disabled internal scheduler when running in cloud mode (delegating probing to the Runner).

### Infrastructure (infra/)
- New Module: infra/modules/dynamodb_targets to provision the Targets table.
- Permissions: Added aws_iam_role_policy to both runner and ecs_api modules to grant dynamodb:* (read/write) access to the - Targets and Results tables.
- Environment: Injected TABLE_NAME_TARGETS and TABLE_NAME_RESULTS into the ECS and Lambda configurations.

### Testing & Verification
- Local Integration Test: Added apps/api/integration_test.go and docker-compose.yml to spin up a local DynamoDB and verify the full flow (Add Target -> Probe -> Save Result).
- Unit Tests: Updated apps/api/main_test.go to be compatible with the refactored code.

Verification
```bash
 go build ./apps/api (Passes)
 go build ./apps/runner (Passes)
 go test ./apps/api/integration_test.go (Passes with local DynamoDB)
 terraform validate (Passes)
```

How to Test Locally
```bash
docker-compose up -d
go test -v ./apps/api/integration_test.go****
```
